## The first or anterior humor of the eye.

<image-desc>A diagram illustrating the classification and properties of the first humor of the eye. It uses curly braces to group related concepts and descriptions, showing its names, substance, quantity, multiplication, location, and uses.</image-desc>
<margin>It is called</margin> { Aqueous <note>Watery</note>. } { from its likeness to water or the white of eggs.
{ Albugineous <note>White-like</note>.

It has a substance thinner than the others.
In quantity, it is quite small compared to the others that follow. Hence its size is indicated by ʒ. fig. 10.15. & 19. Tab. 15.
It is multiplied from an external source; for it has been gathered by observation that if this humor is exhausted, either by a wound or in the cure of a Cataract, it is nevertheless regenerated again within a few days. Indeed, it has its nourishment from the source of the vitreous womb and the *Aranea* <note>The arachnoid or lens capsule</note>, and it is esteemed as that serous and excrementitious <note>waste-product</note> humor which remains from the nourishment of the Crystalline humor. The causes of this are indicated by ʒ. fig. 19. Tab. 15.
<margin>Which</margin> Is situated in the anterior part of the eye, namely between the Uvea membrane (by which this humor is contained) and the Cornea. From which it follows that cataracts are produced within it. For this, see ʒ. fig. 1. Tab. 15. The seat where the vitreous is distinguished from the aqueous by the intervention of the *hyaloid* <note>the glass-like membrane</note> is indicated by ʒ. fig. 10. Tab. 15.

<margin>It has a twofold use</margin> { First, that it distends the Cornea and makes it swell out, and by this way it is made to stand apart from the Crystalline humor; for by this reasoning the pupil always stands in its natural dilation, without which vision would be hindered.
Second is, that it becomes an internal medium fit for receiving the visible species <note>term: visible species; the "images" or "forms" of objects traveling through the air to the eye</note>. Hence it happens that in those approaching death, the cornea becomes hidden and flaccid because of the drying up of this kind of humor; and then a web seems to appear before the eyes of the sick person; for because of the defect of this humor, the visible species cannot be received by the Crystalline, due to the excessive constriction of the pupil, and the cause of its scarcity is the consumption of the animal spirits <note>term: animal spirits; a hypothesized fluid in the nerves responsible for sensation and movement</note> brought about by disease.

## The second or middle humor.

<image-desc>A diagram illustrating the classification and properties of the second humor of the eye. It uses curly braces to group related concepts and descriptions, showing its names, substance, shape, location, and uses.</image-desc>
<margin>The humor is named</margin> { Crystalloid. } { Because it shines like Crystal.
{ Crystalline.

It enjoys a somewhat hard substance, not unlike Camphor.

<margin>This humor is very soft</margin> It has a shape that is in some way spherical, but yet in the
{ Anterior part, which looks toward the aqueous humor or the pupil, it is more depressed and tends somewhat toward flatness. For this, see u. fig. 11. 14 & 20. Tab. 15.
Posterior part, which looks toward the [vitreous] humor, it is observed to bear the likeness of a lens. For this, see ʒ. fig. 4. 12. 13. 14. & 16. Tab. 15.
Moreover, it is in color like white and pellucid Crystal, and if it is removed from its seat and applied over written letters in the manner of a magnifying glass, it will show them far larger than they truly are. And from here, without doubt, those spectacles appropriate for the elderly were invented.

It is situated toward the anterior and almost in the center of the eye, so that the vitreous humor embraces its posterior part, while its anterior front is covered by the *Aranea* tunic <note>The lens capsule</note>. For this, see ʒ. fig. 1. Tab. 15. For the width of the Crystalloid, see ʒ. fig. 12. & 15. Tab. 15.

<margin>It has most eminent and excellent uses in the optical faculty, whence</margin> { It is esteemed the principal organ of the faculty of seeing.
{ It is not inaptly called the idol and image of vision.
{ It can be called the great light of the visible world no differently than the Sun of the greater world, or the heart of the human world.

## The third or final humor.

It is called the humor { **Hyaloid** <note>original: *Hialoides*, meaning glass-like</note> } { Inasmuch as it resembles
                                { **Vitreous** <note>original: *Vitreus*, meaning glassy</note> } { **molten glass**.

It possesses a substance that is not as firm or clear as that of the Crystalline humor <note>The lens</note>.
It is nourished by the **retina** <note>The "net-like" membrane</note>, next to which it has its site and position.
In quantity, it is by far the largest of the three humors, as it seems to claim for itself three out of the four parts of the eye's cavity. From this it is quite clear that it contains the greater part of the Crystalline humor within its own concavity. The **Hyaloid** <note>glass-like</note> indicates the cavity receiving the Crystalline in figure 9, Table 15, marked with *r*. Its size is indicated by *x* in figures 10 and 20, Table 15, and by *β* in figure 18.
<margin>Which</margin> Has its location toward the posterior part of the eye; indeed, this humor is so large that it even extends toward the anterior portion of the eye. This humor, together with the Crystalline, is contained and wrapped by the **arachnoid tunic** <note>original: *tunica aranea*, meaning the "spider-web" membrane; today known as the lens capsule</note>. For this, see *b* in figure 1, Table 15.
It has a brilliant and pleasing appearance to behold, as it is the nourishment (as has been said) for the most clear and transparent Crystalline; and in comparison to other things, it is not inaptly compared to molten glass, both in respect to its color and its viscous tenacity.
It is considered most useful for the power of sight, insofar as it is observed to provide food and nourishment to the Crystalline humor; and in the process of such nutrition, the **albugineous** <note>white or aqueous</note> humor is believed or imagined to be produced as a surplus and serous waste product, much like an excrement <note>In the sense of a biological byproduct</note>.

->PREFACE.<-

### ON THE HIDDEN PERFECTION OF MAN, and his wonderful properties, and the cause of his exaltation and depression.

---

<margin>Archangelus <note>Archangelus de Burgonovo, a 16th-century Franciscan friar known for his commentaries on Cabalistic texts.</note></margin>
<margin>Pico della Mirandola, book 4.</margin>
<margin>Archangelus Paul.</margin>
<margin>Psalm 8:5.</margin>
<image-desc>Historiated woodcut initial 'T' depicting a figure seated in a landscape, possibly a scholar or saint, within a square frame decorated with foliage.</image-desc>The nature of man is so wonderful that he is called the "node" <note>original: "nodus"; meaning a knot or connecting point</note> not only of earthly things, but even of heavenly ones. For this reason, Pico della Mirandola rightly says that *earthly things are entrusted to man, and heavenly things favor him, insofar as his soul is heaven itself, his body is earth, and the link joining these two together is the intermediary spirit.* And from this, the said Pico judged that whatever was said by Moses in the first chapter of Genesis concerning the **Macrocosm** <note>The "Large World" or the universe as a whole.</note> can also be understood concerning man himself, who for this reason is not unwisely called the **Microcosm** <note>The "Little World"; the idea that a human being mirrors the structure of the universe.</note> and "every creature." 

God, being of a better nature, composed man from the mud of the earth and the breath of life so that he might look toward the earth for the health of his body and toward heaven for the salvation of his soul. For, by the secret decree of the immense Creator of all things, such a commerce was ordained between these two extremes that the specimen of the divine likeness—which by its own nature was accustomed to ignore gross things and was not at all inflamed by earthly desire—was covered in a dark garment or earthly house by means of the intermediary spirit. Thus, he forged man, the most noble creature, so that man himself, made into a rational animal from both an eternal and a mortal nature, could satisfy both sides of his origin: both to wonder at and pray to heavenly things, and to inhabit and govern earthly things. 

And by the grace of this immortal and heavenly gift, Archangelus, in his Cabalistic commentaries, recognizes that a divine race indeed dwells in men—or rather, that the soul is like the "seed of God" infused within us. He seems to have received this doctrine from Saint Paul, who confidently proclaimed the *external man to be the temple of the Holy Spirit.* Hence, it was for this reason that the royal prophet <note>Refers to King David, the traditional author of the Psalms.</note> affirmed that *man was created by God a little lower than the angels, crowned with glory and honor, having dominion over the works of His hands, and putting all things under his feet—namely, flocks and herds, the beasts of the field, the birds of the air, and the fish of the sea.* Indeed, even his steps are established by Jehovah... <note>original: "Iehoua"</note>

...is guided by Him <note>referring to God</note>, whose way He delights in; though he falls, he shall not be utterly cast down, because the Lord sustains his hand. He is present with man from his very birth and formation, and has crafted him most skillfully with His wisdom.
<margin>Proverbs 8</margin>
His delights and pleasures are also with the sons of men; for divine wisdom teaches them what is pleasing and acceptable to God. To them, He has kindly revealed the *knowledge and science of the world's composition, the powers of the elements, the beginning, end, and middle of times, the solstices, the changes and variety of seasons and storms, the circuit of the year, the positions of the stars, the natures of living creatures, the dispositions or rages of wild beasts, the forces of winds or spirits, the thoughts of men, and all other things, whether hidden or manifest.*
<margin>Wisdom 7:17</margin>
All these gifts God has granted to man through the Holy Spirit of His wisdom, out of love for the God-like soul <note>original: "animæ Deiformis"</note>. This soul is a thing so noble and adorned with such great dignity and sublimity that, through its mediation—even while veiled by the shadow of the flesh—we may reach the discourse of heavenly angels, the works of God, the progressions of nature, the signs of good things, and the knowledge of divine power, as Mercurius Trismegistus <note>Hermes Trismegistus, a legendary Hellenistic figure associated with ancient wisdom and the "as above, so below" philosophy.</note> bears witness.
<margin>Mercurius Trismegistus, page 3</margin>
But indeed, the dark mass of the earthly body attempts in every way to diminish this happiness of the human soul. It endeavors to entice the soul away from the contemplation of God and divine things toward the allurements of the world and the flesh, by means of the aerial spirit of the blood. Thus, by deceiving the soul through flattery and veiling it in clouds of darkness, the body easily seduces it from the nature of a good spirit <note>original: "boni dæmonis"</note> to the disposition of an evil one <note>original: "cacodæmonis"</note>. By this, man—who by the power of the mind presiding over him should be placed above every creature—is now rendered equal to the beast, and indeed made viler than the brute itself, as one who is now imbued and contaminated by the filth and pollution of sin.
<margin>Job 14</margin>
Hence it has happened that this creature, most eminent in respect to the breath of God-like life, has now become rotten and most vile by reason of the body; as Job also seems to recognize in this series of words: *Man decays like a rotten thing, like a garment consumed by moths; man born of woman is of few days and full of trouble,* <margin>Psalm 77:39</margin> that is, he is filled with many miseries. Similarly, in respect to the body, man is called flesh, *a spirit <note>or breath/wind</note> that passes away and does not return.* <margin>Job 26</margin> For this reason, he is also called by Job *rottenness and a mortal, and his son a worm or an earthworm.*
<margin>Wisdom 1</margin>
Yet God made both the external and internal man upright and most temperate: for He Himself *did not place death and transgression upon the earth, nor does He delight in the destruction of the living; for He created all things that they might exist, and He made the nations of the world healthy.* But *injustice, or sin, is the acquisition of death: For justice (which is always with God) is immortal,* <margin>Wisdom 2</margin> by which God fashioned man *immortal, and according to the image of His own likeness. But through the envy of the Devil, Death entered into the world.*
Therefore, human unhappiness was introduced by the Devil, the prince of darkness; just as supreme and eternal beatitude was brought to man by God, the source of light and the Ruler of justice, through the gift of the mind, and complete washing from the filth of sin through the blood of Christ. By Divine blessing, therefore, so great was the dignity of Adam in the breath of innocence, and so exalted was his honor, that he stood immortal; indeed, he was equal to the angels themselves. Hence, even after his fall, the angel remembers this same nobility when he would not allow man to offer him any reverence or adoration, as is declared in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation.</note>. <margin>Apocalypse</margin>
Finally, as we have called him the "node" <note>the knot or junction point</note> of all things in the preceding sections, so also in this place we call him, in a certain way, the "end" <note>or final purpose</note> of all things. For he who adheres to God in his mind matches the angels in reason, aspires to the sun through the life of his heart, regards the brutes or irrational animals through his sensory powers, is related to the plant in his natural forces, and has a connection to inanimate things in his body. <margin>1 Chronicles</margin> Therefore, on account of this singularity, all creatures of the earth, sea, and air are subjected to his dominion, and that by divine command.
Wonderful and most hidden, therefore, are the mysteries of man, both internal and external, and beyond the grasp of the common man. Indeed, at first glance they seem impossible, and the secret operation of the mind, the soul, and the aerial spirit diffused within man is ineffable; likewise, it is difficult to explain with the subtleties of words, and therefore it is much more impossible to [reveal] these parts of the internal man with the edge of a scalpel, as...

# PREFACE.

...and by whatever right hand <note>original: "cunque dextra"</note> to divide or segregate them from each other; Nay, indeed, *it belongs to the word of God alone* (as we have from Saint Paul <note>A reference to Hebrews 4:12: "For the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing to the division of soul and spirit."</note>) *to distinguish the spirit from the soul*. # SECTION I.
## PORTION III.
### PART III.
# **BOOK ONE**
# IN WHICH THE NORTHERN AND SOUTHERN BLASTS OF THE WINDS IN THE MICROCOSM—THAT IS, THE WINDS OF THE SPLEEN AND THE LIVER—AND THEIR EFFECTS ARE EXPLAINED.
## CHAPTER I.

->Concerning the four cardinal angles of the Microcosm, concerning its poles: and how, and how aptly, it is adapted to the Macrocosm in its position.<-

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'V' with scrolling foliage and floral motifs.</image-desc>VARIOUS are the opinions of philosophers, both Pagans and Christians, regarding the position of the Macrocosm <note>term: Macrocosm; the "great world" or the universe as a whole.</note>, which the Microcosm <note>term: Microcosm; the "little world," referring to man as a reflection of the universe.</note> is observed to imitate no differently than a son imitates his father. For the Microcosm (as Hermes Trismegistus <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure to whom many mystical and philosophical works were attributed.</note> testifies) is the son of the Macrocosm, just as the Macrocosm is the offspring of God Himself. Hence, it is impossible to investigate the cardinal points and angles of the Microcosm or man—and especially his poles—except through a fit application of the same to his father, namely the greater world. However, to find the exact location of the right and left sides of the world is a matter not so easily accomplished, since in the inquiry into this, the industry of the sharpest philosophers has been not only irregular, but even their minds on this matter <margin>Pythagoras, Plato, Aristotle, Empedocles.</margin> remain uncertain and inconsistent to this very day. For Pythagoras, Plato, and Aristotle placed the right side of the world at the Eastern region because (they say) the motion of the world begins from that quarter. But Empedocles, by no means adhering to this opinion of theirs, extends the right hand of the world toward the summer solstice—that is, toward the Tropic of Cancer—and consequently extends its left toward the winter, and by this reasoning, comparing the world with man, it is necessary that his face look toward the Western region of the world; whereas according to the assertion of the aforementioned men, he would look toward the North. What then is to be done in such great controversy, except to flee to the sacred and true oracle of God, and elicit the truth of this matter from His response?

In many places in the sacred scriptures, we find that in the prayers of the prophets and patriarchs, and in the <margin>Matthew 24:27; Numbers 35:5.</margin> formula for praying, the face of the one praying was always arranged toward the East. And in Matthew we read that lightning comes from the east and moves toward the west; and elsewhere we have: *Measure toward the Eastern region, and toward the Southern region, and toward the Western region, and toward the Northern region.* It is as if he had said: measure toward the front part, the right, the left, and <margin>Job 23:8.</margin> the back. Furthermore, this point is confirmed by Job in the passage dealing with the search for the place or seat of Jehovah, which is interpreted thus by Pagninus <note>Sante Pagnini (1470–1536), a Dominican friar and leading Hebraist who produced a literal Latin translation of the Bible.</note>: *Behold, I shall go to the East, and He will not be there; and to the West, and I shall not perceive Him; or to the North while He works, and I shall not see Him; He hides Himself in the south, and I shall not see Him.* But Jerome <note>Saint Jerome (c. 342–420 AD), the primary translator of the Latin Vulgate Bible.</note> interprets this passage thus: *If I go to the East, He appears not; if to the West, I shall not understand Him; if to the left, what shall I do? I shall not catch Him; if I turn myself to the right, I shall not see Him.* Tremellius <note>Immanuel Tremellius (1510–1580), a Jewish convert to Christianity and a renowned Hebraist.</note> translates that passage in this sense: *If I go forward, He will not be present; if backward, I shall not notice Him; when He acts on the left, yet I shall not see Him; He will cover the right region, yet I shall not behold Him.* 

Therefore, what Pagninus makes the Eastern angle of the world, Tremellius makes the front part; what the former makes the Western quarter, the latter makes the back; what that man calls the North, this man calls the left hand of the world, just as he also called the right region of this world the South. From these things (as it seems to me) it appears without any controversy that the correct arrangement of man according to the position of the world is with his face disposed toward the eastern region, whence the eyes are placed in the front part of man and of all other creatures (namely, the face), so that they might greet the rising Sun—visiting the dark earth from the east with its golden and bright aspect after the long night and darkness, and banishing the gloom of the night into exile—as a type <note>In theology, a "type" is a person or event in the Old Testament or nature that foreshadows something in the New Testament or the divine realm.</note> of the invisible Sun, whom the Holy Bible predicted would come from that part of the world on the last day for the renewal of the world. Hence...

...Therefore it follows that his hand or right side faces the South, just as the left faces the North, and consequently his posterior part must look toward the West. Since this is the case, it is necessary that we seek in the left region of man, or the Microcosm <note>term: Microcosm; the "little world," a Renaissance concept that the human body is a miniature map of the entire universe.</note>, that Arctic pole from which Boreas <note>The personification of the North wind.</note> sends forth his cold and earthy blasts into the little world. And also we must seek the pole opposite to it, namely the Antarctic, which must necessarily be investigated in his right side. The Eastern part of man is the anterior portion of the Chest, toward which the cone of the heart (which is the Sun of the little world) inclines, just as his western region is in the back part, where the seminal vessels, kidneys, and bladder are immersed in the "midst of the earth," that is, the mass of the intestines.

# CHAPTER II.

## *Concerning the investigation of the two poles of the Microcosm, and that they are the Spleen and the Liver.*

Since the disposition of man is found to be such in relation to the disposition of the world—that his left side corresponds to the northern region of the Macrocosm <note>term: Macrocosm; the "great world" or the universe at large.</note>—we must discern through diligent inquiry which part in the northern region of the little world is endowed with such properties that it agrees in almost all respects with the Arctic or Northern pole of the greater world. As for the nature of the Macrocosmic North, the effects of the wind blowing from it denote that it is the coldest and driest quarter of the world; its nature is to freeze and harden both earth and water with its coldness and dryness, and to produce ice, snow, and hail. Furthermore, by its cold and dry nature, it thins, constricts, contracts, and makes things wrinkled or rough; it takes away action and numbs; it destroys fruits and flowers, dries up herbs, and affects humors both internal and external, performing all such things through its Northern blast.

In the left corner of man, we find almost nothing of significance except the Spleen <note>original: *Lien*</note>, whose nature we perceive does not differ much from that of the polar star if we explore the matter a little more accurately. For since its nature is earthy, it is the coldest and driest portion of the entire lower region. It sends forth cold and dry winds into the whole region of the little world just as the North wind does from its own quarter. Similarly, by its blasts, it freezes and hardens humors, produces glassy and thick phlegm, creates icy viscosities, constricts dross-like matter, and disperses melancholy <note>term: Melancholy; one of the four "humors" or bodily fluids in ancient medicine, characterized as cold, dry, and earthy.</note> everywhere. Melancholy is nothing other than earthy matter, cold and dry, which it freezes into hardness, just as Boreas by his blast thickens the tender airy humor into snow and hail. By its bodily dryness, it thins things, just as Northern cold constricts and contracts soft earth; it brings forth numbness and paralysis. To put it briefly, it is that member of the body which brings greater harm to human life than any other in the entire body, insofar as it participates in the nature of Saturn <note>The planet Saturn was traditionally called the "Greater Malefic" in astrology, associated with cold, old age, and decay.</note>, which is the greater misfortune. Indeed, it is opposed to life in every way, because by its extreme cold it is most opposed to innate heat, and by its dryness it is most opposed to the radical moisture <note>term: Radical Moisture; the vital fluid believed to be the fuel for the "lamp of life."</note>. Furthermore, the agreement between this organ and the polar star is declared in this: that both claim Saturn for their constellation, from whom they have their styptic <note>contracting or binding</note> virtues. But truly, because man is called the "son of the world," he receives that force from the Angel presiding over the North wind (under whose care is also the sphere of Saturn), and the spleen of the little world likewise draws its power from the North wind, whence both produce the same effects.

By a similar reasoning, as the cardinal wind opposite the North is called Auster <note>The South wind.</note>, it breathes forth moist and warm blasts from the southern pole. In the greater world, it is observed to make the air gross and thick with its spirit, sometimes producing lightning, and most often bringing and multiplying rain. As our Hippocrates <note>The "Father of Medicine," whose theories on the environment and health were foundational.</note> confesses, this very wind opens the pores of the body, hinders the power of feeling, and creates heaviness in the body. It diminishes hearing and makes it difficult, affects the head with pain, dissolves the humors of the body and moves them from the interior to the exterior parts; indeed, it induces numbness in the senses and destroys them, generating diseases such as gout <note>original: *podagra*</note>, epilepsy, itching, and fevers. 

Nevertheless, its natural virtue is quite healthful, insofar as it makes hard things soft. It is also sometimes the author of benevolent dew and moderate rain, by which it softens and opens the pores of the earth and makes it fruitful, whence it brings forth, nourishes, and causes fruits, herbs, grasses, and seeds to grow. It dissolves thick and cold humors, and causes vapors and superfluous humors to flow out through sweat from the bodies of both plants and animals. 

Thus, one must also seek and explore in that part of the human body directly opposite the Spleen on the axis something that can be compared in all things to this southern corner, from which the "microcosmic South wind" is accustomed to blow—either with a preternatural effect or a natural and expected success. By due inquiry, we find the Liver <note>original: *Hepar*</note> to be such a thing in the right side of the little world, which is most aptly compared to the southern corner not only in position but also in property. For first, the axis of this region—namely the liver—tends directly to the center of the Spleen, just as the axis of the Antarctic pole tends to the Arctic or Northern one. Secondly, the liver in its nature is warm and moist, and it emits such blasts into the little world as the South wind does from the southern region of the Macrocosm. Furthermore, it turns air into healthful dewy and bloody clouds, by which the whole "human earth" is irrigated, every member of the same is nourished, and generation and growth are completed. Humors condensed and congealed by the cold of the Northern wind (the Spleen) are dissipated and expelled through the pores in sweat (mediated by its benevolent heat), and thus, in the manner of a well-ordered Macrocosmic South wind, all things are ordained for life according to the laws of nature. 

At such a time, Jupiter <note>The planet Jupiter was the "Greater Benefic," associated with expansion, warmth, and health.</note> is present as a benevolent and favoring foster-father to both the macrocosmic and microcosmic South winds. But truly, if Mars <note>The planet of excessive heat, fire, and inflammation.</note> mixes himself with its temperament, whether in the macrocosm or the microcosm, then preternatural blasts of this kind will follow: dense clouds will be raised up by the intemperance of heat and will be converted into catarrhs and defluxions in the manner of worldly rain and floods. Heaviness of the head will be generated, along with numbness of the senses and other infirmities which the worldly South wind is accustomed to bring forth—namely gout, epilepsy, and itching. Indeed, if the influence of Mars upon it is even a little more...

## CHAPTER III.

### Concerning the specific "weather events" arising from the Spleen, and their comparison with those blown from the Macrocosmic North Wind. Concerning the primary cause of the North wind in the Great World, from which the Spleen receives its power.

IN the previously mentioned series of words, it has been clearly enough declared that the Spleen, by its position in the human body, corresponds to the Northern Pole of the world. Whether it also agrees with that region in its disposition and property will be explained from what follows. The Northern part is indeed very cold and dry by its quality, and for this reason, 
<margin>Job 37:9</margin> it is observed to produce such winds or blasts, according to that passage of the sacred scriptures: *North winds produce cold.* <note>original: "Venti Aquilonares producunt frigus." This is a reference to the Latin Vulgate Bible.</note>
<margin>Prov. 25:23</margin> Furthermore, that such a wind is exceedingly dry is explained therein, *because it is said by Solomon himself to drive away and scatter the rains*, which it would by no means accomplish unless it were most opposed to the moisture of the rains. Therefore, just as the Northern corner of the world is a Cardinal wind, a cold and dry receptacle for the same, so also is the Spleen (or the "North" of man) of such a quality, as it is the seat of melancholy, which enjoys an earthy disposition—that is, cold and dry. For this reason, Northern blasts—namely cold and dry ones—are emitted from this cardinal point of the microcosm <note>term: Microcosm; the human body viewed as a miniature version of the universe.</note>, stirring up unnatural passions in the lesser world no differently than the North wind (Boreas) or the Arctic wind does in the greater world. For just as the North sometimes emits snow and hail by itself, and produces frost, and is sometimes armed with tremendous thunder, so also—sometimes by raw winds prone to acidity, which bring on a viscous and "glassy" phlegm <note>term: glassy phlegm (pituita vitrea); a medical term for thick, clear mucus thought to be caused by cold.</note> and freeze it into a mucosal substance—cachexia <note>term: cachexia; a state of ill health and malnutrition.</note> and other foul habits of the body are produced. Numbness and torpor are created throughout the whole frame; Epilepsy, Paralysis, Apoplexy, and other things of this kind are procreated from the condensations of humors and vapors. Similarly, two types of watery dropsy <note>term: dropsy; an old term for edema or swelling caused by fluid retention.</note> occur, which is best demonstrated in the scorbutic <note>term: scorbutic; related to scurvy.</note> disposition and in "virgin's affections" <note>note: Likely referring to chlorosis or "green sickness," an anemic condition then attributed to young women.</note>, where the blasts or winds springing from this region are accustomed to freeze the humors into an icy substance. These frozen humors then block the passages, and the blocked passages often procreate foul dispositions of the body. And these types of Northern "windiness" happen in the microcosm with thunder or a murmur and rumbling, as if spirits are within them (according to the nature of those who inhabit the clouds driven by the violence of the winds from the world's North), which accompany those men whose melancholy for the most part arises from burnt phlegm. This is clearly observed in hypochondriacs and those afflicted with tympanites <note>term: tympanites; a condition where the abdomen is stretched tight like a drum due to gas.</note>. Alternatively, they happen without thunder or evident belching, and then the phlegmatic humor has been made more acidic and glassy; this humor is likened to the snow and frost procreated by the North winds in winter time, which intense coldness accompanies. And this is that humor, thickened by the cold and dry Splenic winds, which is frequently accustomed to produce numbness, torpor, and Epileptic passions, as it is a place where humors and evil spirits enjoy hiding—spirits which are of the nature of those who flee the light, and who freeze in the manner of earthy cold and dryness. Such also are those Northern spirits which, driven from the North wind toward the South, constrict the air condensed into snow and hail by their earthy cold, and congeal the terrestrial waters into frost. But the blasts arising from the mass of the melancholy humor radiating within man are likened to those which are observed to blow from the Northern region of the world during summer, carrying with them a certain fiery breath, hail-filled and dry clouds, and most full of lightning. These bring damage, fears, and inexpressible sadness both to the earth and its fruits, as well as to animals. From this it happens that men oppressed by this kind of melancholy blast fall into Phrenitis <note>term: Phrenitis; an acute delirium or inflammation of the brain.</note>, Lycanthropy <note>term: Lycanthropy; a delusion where a patient believes they have turned into a wolf.</note>, and infinite other vexations of furious melancholy. It must be understood first, therefore, that there is a twofold beginning of unnatural melancholy: namely, either excessive "adustion" <note>term: adustion; the "burning" or overheating of the bodily humors.</note>—just as wood is first turned into coals by a fiery nature and afterward reduced to the state of ashes—so bile is reduced to "black bile" or a coal-like and ashy nature. This species is that which accompanies lightning, which converts fiery substance into ashes and salts, as can be seen in a "thunder-stone." So also this melancholy, with inflammation preceding it, hardens the spleen, and when its earthy exhalation is mixed with fire, the brain is damaged, the imagination is deceived, and reason itself is alienated. This is caused by the foul spirits carried in that sweltering cloud, who lead men away in an insane
<margin>End of Medicine, 12.</margin> manner and render them furious. And this is why Galen says, *Typhomania is a lethargic delirium.* <note>note: Typhomania was a historical term for a state of stupor mixed with low-grade delirium.</note> But in truth, this species of melancholy never happens from the Spleen by itself, except where there is a confluence of foul spirits springing from the Liver, which is suffering from a hot and sweltering imbalance, along with a most dry blast tending toward heat which is ejected from the spleen. The second principle of melancholy is "mortification" or freezing, and its beginning is not inflammation or burning, but conversely, coldness, rawness, and an extreme lack of heat. This species is attributed to that Northern part of the world which ends in clouds of hail and snow, endowed with extreme cold, with no fiery meteor mixing in. But melancholy produced from burnt phlegm seems to participate in both of these extremes, and for this reason, melancholics of this species...

An imbalance of this kind is followed by a **quartan fever** <note>A type of malaria where the fever recurs every fourth day, historically associated with "black bile" and the spleen.</note>, accompanied by a humor with which malignant spirits of that same condition mix themselves. These things (I say) must be understood regarding the **Spleen** and its "winds" <note>Referring to vapors or gases produced by the organ.</note> when they are poorly and unnaturally disposed—either by themselves or by reason of some contrary, malevolent wind—distorted and changed from their natural state into its opposite. For just as the North Wind of the world is observed to bring many benefits to the air and is healthy in itself—since, when well-disposed, it renders the air clear and pure by its blast, dissipates southern clouds, and consequently opposes the plague that arises from the South—so too we see that the wind gently and sweetly emitted from the **Spleen**, and the humor carried by it into the parts of the body, usually brings more health than disease to it. 

From this arises its ability to dry up superfluous humors in the body, oppose putrefaction, and dissipate and dissolve the vapors unnaturally raised by the "Hepatic South" <note>The author compares the Liver (Hepar) to the warm, moist South.</note>, mitigating unnatural heats by its blast and creating a proper balance. Part of a famous medieval hexameter: "The heart glows, the lung speaks, the bile moves anger, the spleen makes one laugh, the liver forces one to love."</note> Furthermore, its acidic vapor is the author of appetite and of the retentive or restrictive faculty, as the fathers of both Physicians and Philosophers testify. 

Concerning the collateral winds of the north, such as the *Aquilo* or *Boreas* <note>Traditional names for the North and Northeast winds.</note>, which are observed to blow from the Polar axis toward the East, and are compared to the wind blowing from the upper hollow region of the Spleen; as well as the wind called *Corus* <note>The Northwest wind.</note> in the **macrocosm** <note>The "Great World" or universe.</note>, which in man usually blows from the hump of the Spleen and tends to inflate that region (namely from the left hypochondrium); I have proposed elsewhere in the second section—where supernatural causes of diseases will be treated—to discuss this openly and quite copiously. In the following chapter, we shall speak of it, albeit sparingly. It remains in this place, however, for us to elicit the primary causes of these winds, first in the world, and then in man.

We Christians say, therefore, contrary to the doctrine of **Hippocrates**, **Avicenna**, and the rest of the Pagans, that the cause of this or that disease is **God**. This was indeed abundantly explained in Part 1, Book 3, Chapters 1, 2, and 3 of this first section, concerning supersubstantial principles. For hence it is said: *Good and evil, life and death, poverty and honor are from God* <note>Sirach/Ecclesiasticus 11:14.</note>; and elsewhere, *The Lord has power over life and death; he leads down to the gates of death and brings back again.* And **Moses** testifies to this same thing in these words: *Jehovah will make the pestilence cling to you until he consumes you; Jehovah will strike you with consumption, and with a fever, and with the burning ulcer of Egypt, and with hemorrhoids, and with the scab, and with the itch, of which you cannot be healed.* Similarly, we learn from **Job**: *That Jehovah rebukes through pain upon the bed.* And among us, it is a familiar idea that God has brought this or that evil upon us for our sins. 

We must ask, therefore, with diligent intuition: how does God usually afflict sinners with diseases and plague? Is it, for instance, immediately, or through the mediation of his other creatures? In **David**, we read: *Angels of God, most mighty in strength, performing his word, listening to the voice of his word, his armies and ministers, doing his pleasure.* And elsewhere these angels are called the winds or *spirits of God*, whence it is read: *Who makes your angels spirits* (as **Jerome** interprets it) or *winds* (as **Tremellius** <note>Immanuel Tremellius, a 16th-century converted Jewish scholar known for his Latin translation of the Bible.</note> maintains) *and your ministers a burning fire.* From this it is clear that when God is said to do this or that, it is done by primary ordination, and not by immediate execution; for whatever is ordained by God, whether to affect one with good or to infest one with punishment or a plague, all that is usually executed by angels as his ministers. Hence it is said: *the angels of God shall give command concerning the just.* And **Josephus** <note>Referring to the Jewish historian Flavius Josephus.</note> says: *May that Angel who rescues me from every evil bless these boys.* But truly, on the opposite side, it is said: *The Angel would have killed Balaam with a sword, had his donkey not turned away from his sight.* Similarly, David saw the Angel of God devastating with a plague and afflicting with a deadly disease; furthermore, it was the Devil who, by the ordination of God, inflicted the plague upon Job. From these things, it is evident that God acts by ordination, and the Angels by execution in these lower realms, whether for life and health, or for death and disease. Consequently, it is clear that angels, and the demons ordained under their command, are the intermediate agents between God and lower things,

But in truth, we must agree with the philosophers on this: namely, that wind is nothing other than a fluctuating motion of the air. Instead, we say that wind is **formal**, which is an angelic spirit sent by God, which so disturbs the air; which air, thus commoted, the philosophers (looking at the exterior and by no means reaching the interior) called "wind." ...to his ministers, who dwell in the turbulent air; but let us hasten thus to the proof of this matter.

Just as seven princes of the angels are numbered who stand before Jehovah—as we gather from the words of the angels Raphael and Gabriel in the books of **Tobit** and **Daniel**—so those more skilled in **Occult Theosophy** <note>original: *Theosophia occulta*</note> and the **Cabala** <note>A Jewish mystical tradition often adapted by Renaissance Christian scholars like Fludd to explain the structure of the universe.</note> have made these seven angels the rulers over the seven **Planets**. They have also assigned the dominion of the four corners or regions of the world to four of these princes: specifically, the Eastern Corner to **Michael**, the Western to **Raphael**, the Northern to **Gabriel**, and the Southern to **Uriel**. These are the "good presidents" who possess power and governance over the winds, of whom the Cabalists have written: *Angels or demons are called spirits, insofar as they are like winds.* Hence **Rabbi Thedacus Levi**, in his book on the ten numerations, after mentioning the North, South, East, and West winds, continues by saying: *And for those four winds He created four Angels who are set over them by day and by night. Michael, who is of the side of mercy and compassion, is appointed over the East wind until midday; Raphael, who is likewise of the side of mercy, rules the West wind; then Gabriel, by the power of judgment and severity, is set over the North wind; and Horiel (whom others call Uriel) presides over the South.* He further asserts that each of these contains many species or legions beneath them. In the *Gate of Light* <note>original: *Porta lucis*, likely the *Sha'are Orah* by Joseph Gikatilla, a fundamental Cabalistic text.</note>, it is read that from the earth up to the firmament there is no empty space, but everything is full of forms. Some of these are pure, capable of grace and mercy; others, it is said, are many foul, harmful, and tempting images below, all of which are described as dwelling and flying in the air. Some are for peace, others for war; some for good, others for evil; some for life, and others for death—and this is confirmed by **Joseph Castaliensis** <note>Giuseppe Castiglione, an Italian scholar.</note>. 

But to proceed, the purely named princes who preside over the four corners have four spirits beneath them who are said to be the immediate leaders of the cardinal winds, to whom it is given to harm the earth and the sea. Those deeper in the mysteries of nature have called these **Orient**, **Paymon**, **Egyn**, and **Amonium**. The first is said to govern the wind of the dawn (the East wind); the second governs **Favonius** (the West wind) in the western corner; the third governs the North; and the last governs **Auster** (the South wind) in the South. And it is undoubtedly regarding these spirits that this passage of the 

<margin>Revelation 7</margin>
**Apocalypse** <note>The Book of Revelation.</note> is understood: *I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree. And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God: and he cried with a loud voice to the four angels, to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea, saying, Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.* From this we can elicit, first, that four malignant angels are ordained by God, under the command of the good ones, for the governance of the cardinal winds. Second, that malignant angels are accustomed to harm the earth and its creatures by means of the winds or the medium of the air. Third, that they cannot hasten to the ruin or harm of sublunary creatures beyond the permission of the Divine Majesty. Finally, it appears that this angel, whom those four spirits seemed to obey, is **Michael**, the leader of the heavenly host, whom the Cabalists call **Metatron** <note>original: *Metattron*</note>. They say this was the Angel who preceded Moses in the desert, in whom the name of the living God was impressed, as is read in **Exodus**. For this reason, he is called here the Priest of Heaven, who is also the leader of the army of Christ. **Archangelus** <note>referring to Archangelus of Borgonovo, a Cabalistic commentator.</note>, in his *Cabalistic Dogmas*, affirms that he fights with his angels against the ancient serpent for the souls of all. It was likely, therefore, that this was the Angel who imposed the law upon those four malignant Angels, lest they harm the earth until the appointed time—especially because Michael, as the aforementioned Rabbi Tedacus says, is on the side of grace and mercy, and also because once the serpent was conquered by him, the serpent and his angels were made to obey him by force of arms. And yet, Satan continually resists God and His angels with all his might; unless the good angels were constantly present for us by divine permission, the malignant spirits would bring immediate and irrecoverable ruin to the human race, to whom they are most hostile, observing that humanity bears the image of God (whom they hate). 

Hence, we read among the Cabalists that just as there are four standard-bearers in the army of God—namely Michael, Raphael, Gabriel, and Uriel—so also in the army of Satan, **Samael**, **Azazel**, **Azael**, and **Mahazael** carry the widest and darkest banners. Of these, Samael exercises his power in the element of fire, Azazel in the air, Azael in the water, and Mahazael in the earth. These standard-bearers receive their power from the winds or the air, since by their mediation they are accustomed to carry out God's will for evil or punishment, according to that word of the Royal Psalmist:

<margin>Psalm 148</margin>
*The stormy wind fulfilling His word,* where under the name of "wind," one understands both the moved air (which is the external motion of the wind) and the spirit or demon with his 
<margin>Ezekiel 37</margin>
spiritual troops or crowds (who is the internal mover of the wind). Hence **Ezekiel** says, speaking of the resurrection of the bones: *Come from the four winds, O spirit, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live,* where he seems to speak of the good angels. For (as the gloss upon this passage says) *by the spirit from the four winds, the prophet understands the four*
<margin>Daniel 7</margin>
*angelic intelligences* who preside over the four corners of the world. And **Daniel**, speaking of harmful spirits, says: *Behold, the four winds of the heaven strove upon the great sea,* by which he most aptly declares the nature of the winds or the disturbance of the air: namely, that it is nothing other than the contention of spirits of contrary natures in the air. For we see the waves in the sea excited and agitated, and a great disturbance and roar of the waters created, by the violent motion of a multitude of fish, or even by one very large one. 

But someone will object that this cannot happen with the fiery demons who live their lives in the element of fire, nor with those who inhabit the middle region of the air, because in those two spheres of the elementary world, wind (according to the opinion of the philosophers) is not found. But first, I would like to remind those skilled in philosophy that the demons of any element may inhabit any part of the air according to their free will, and are present everywhere according to the permission of God, either for blessing or for punishment. Furthermore (let this be said with all due respect to them), we frequently gather from the Holy Scriptures that wind occurs in the middle region of the air, where we find that God makes the clouds 
<margin>Psalm 104:3</margin>
*His chariot, who walks upon the wings of the wind, who makes His angels winds, and His ministers a flaming fire.* Who also is unaware...

# On Mystical Anatomy.

...does not know that the clouds, which are created and moved in the middle region of the air, are driven by the winds from any quarter of the world toward their opposite. From this it is evident that even the wind—contrary to the opinion of the **Peripatetics** <note>Followers of Aristotle, who believed winds were confined to the lowest part of the atmosphere.</note>—blows not only in the lowest region of the air, but also in the middle and highest regions; indeed, it blows even more in its very center than in its lower part, inasmuch as it drives and moves clouds of every condition before it. Furthermore, we see that clouds gathered by the winds are filled with **demons** <note>In the philosophy of Robert Fludd, 'demons' are spiritual intelligences or 'elementals' that inhabit the air, not necessarily evil spirits.</note>, whose aerial or external force produces noise, while their internal force produces lightning. For the manifest part of demons is air, but their hidden part is fire; from this, therefore, the "marrow" of thunder arises. In the highest region of the air, where the fiery element has its dominion, the wind blows, but not so violently, because it finds less resistance there due to the thinness of the element and the company of the demons dwelling there. These demons, because of their sharpness, have dominion over the coarser demons—namely the watery and earthy ones—and they mix with them and wage war, whereas conversely the watery demons rarely ascend beyond the middle region of the air (in which they wage war with those contrary to them). Thus it happens that we see **comets** generated in this region of the air, which are created from the denser part of that region, or from a more fiery spirit that has become thickened, just as we observe clouds are created from the condensation of air in the middle region. This gathering of aerial parts, both in the middle and highest regions of the air, is usually caused by the blowing of various winds; however, they differ in color according to the disposition of the region and its demons, whether they be watery, aerial, or fiery.

Indeed—to now reveal a great mystery—just as clouds and all other **meteors** <term>meteors: A broad historical term for any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, snow, lightning, and comets.</term> (which are called "imperfect mixtures" by philosophers) are formed by the blowing of opposite or contrary winds, coagulating and condensing the air by their gathering—in which the condensed air is the body, the wind is the spirit, and the soul driving it (carried immediately in the spirit) is a demon or angel—so also it must be understood and concluded that all "perfect mixtures" <note>Solid, stable things like plants, animals, and minerals.</note>, which are constituted from these meteors or imperfect mixtures, have the same internal agents and patients. That is to say: the wind, which is composed of subtle air and angelic light or brilliance, serves either by being hidden in the "belly" of a cloud and driving its spirit and body in the manner of a soul, or by appearing openly and visibly exiting the cloud. From this, it happens that infinite "composites" are found in the nature of things, each of which has within itself contrary natures and properties diverse from one another. This is because that wind—producing the visible world through the power of the Word as its primary "sperm"—is perfected and mixed by the blowing of opposite and side-by-side winds. Its "sperm" or external part is visibly condensed air, but its "seed" (which is its invisible internal part) is born from various demons and spirits, and consequently possesses various natures and properties. 

For example, in **opium** or the juice of the poppy, we perceive a bitter nature, which partakes of bile or fire; yet its pain-relieving <note>original: *annodina*</note> disposition is contrary to heat and fire, inasmuch as it stupifies, takes away sensation, and induces a deep and deadly sleep. Thus it happens that the blowing of the **North Wind** <note>original: *Borealis*</note> prevails in the composition of that particular "meteor." Similarly, we observe **fumitory** <note>A flowering plant used in traditional medicine.</note> to be cold and dry in its operation, and yet we gather from its taste that it is bitter; thus we see that the spirits of different winds or elements are present within it. From here also proceeds the mystery of that property of a thing which is called **occult** <note>Hidden or "unspeakable" qualities that cannot be explained by the four basic elements alone.</note>: namely, from internal demonic forms of this kind, which—because of the various mixing of winds in the meteor's composition—appear to be more hidden and inscrutable.

<margin>Reuchlin, in *On the Art of the Cabala*.</margin>
The **Cabalist** <note>A practitioner of Jewish mysticism; here Fludd refers to Johannes Reuchlin, a Christian scholar of the Cabala.</note> also seems to confirm this in these words: "An Angel is a middle power between God and nature, from which operations are performed in things that their own nature either would not do, or would do differently; which some say come from an 'occult property,' and others simply 'because it is so.'"

From this (I say) comes the reason for the **sympathies and antipathies** <note>Natural attractions or repulsions between objects, like a magnet and iron.</note> of things, with the air acting as the mediator. We conclude, therefore, that from the blowing of the four winds, all things are made that exist in the heavens and the earth. For the first author is God himself, who acts in diverse ways in this world, and according to his various properties in acting, various names are attributed to him—not essential names, but those taken from a property. For although many names are spoken of God, none is truly appropriated to him except one, which is the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH.</note>, as **Rabbi Moses** <note>Maimonides (Moses ben Maimon).</note> testifies; for this denotes the substance of the Creator in a pure sense, in which there is no participation. But his other names denote a thing with participation, by reason or respect of the works or actions performed by him in creation. Thus he is called **Adonai** <note>Lord</note> from his dominion, and consequently the cause of glory and honor; he is also called **Ehies** <note>I Am / Father</note> as a father, or **Cheten** <note>Crown (Keter)</note> as a crown. And **Hochma**, that is, **Wisdom**; and **Bina**, that is, **Prudence**; and **Chesed**, that is, **Clemency**; and **Geburath**, that is, **Punishment**; and **Tiphereth**, which is **Grace**; and **Netreth**, which is **Triumph**; and **Hod**, that is, **Praise**; and **Iesod**, which is **Redemption**; and **Malchad**, which is **Kingdom**. From this it is clear that these are, as it were, his surnames, which are ascribed to him in respect to those actions by which he works here in the world.

And through the first of these attributes, namely the **Crown** <note>original: *Cheten* (Keter)</note>, God rains his will immediately into the orders of the **Seraphim** angels, who commit the matter to the Archangel **Metattron**. He, being the primary prince, pours his influence into the **Primum Mobile** <note>The "first moved" sphere, the outermost sphere of the heavens in the old model of the universe.</note>, from which he rains the material essence of things—that is, the universal water—by the command of the Crown. 

His second name with participation is **Wisdom** <note>original: *Hochma*</note>, which pours its will into the sphere of the **Cherubim** angels; their influence is received by the Archangel **Iophiel**, who transfuses his commands into the **Starry Heaven** as a formal essence, and thus gives life to every creature. 

The third is **Prudence** <note>original: *Binah*</note>, which sends its virtue into the heaven of the **Thrones**; they commit the will of Prudence to the Archangel **Zaphkiel**, and he faithfully commends it here to the angels or demons of the heaven of **Saturn**. These, by the power of the inferior spirits and through the mediation of the air (moved here and there by them), carry out the final execution of the will of Prudence, whether it be for good or for evil. 

The fourth is **Clemency** <note>original: *Chesed*</note>, which sends its decree into the sphere of the **Dominations**; these again commend it to the Archangel **Zadkiel**, who, transfusing it into the heaven of **Jupiter**, causes it to be fatally rained down into lower things by its spirits. There, by the demons swimming in the winds, according to the pleasure of God, it is brought into act...

### Section I. Portion III. Part III. Book I.

...is led: and an influx of this kind tends toward mercy and clemency. The fifth is **Severity** <note>Original: *Geburath* (Gevurah). In the Kabbalah, this represents God's judgment and power.</note>, which denotes punishment and severity; it transmits its effect into the order of **Powers** <note>One of the nine traditional choirs of angels.</note>, from which it is carried downward to the angel **Samael**. He commits this to the fatal demons governing the sphere of **Mars**, by whom it is entrusted to the spirits of the element of **Fire**. These spirits, moving within the winds, fulfill the severe edict of the divine power of Severity.

The sixth is **Grace** <note>Original: *Triphereth* (Tiferet). Often translated as Beauty, it represents balance.</note>, which flows to the **Virtues**, and from them to the Archangel **Michael**. From here, it is passed again to the spirits occupying the sphere of the **Sun**, and finally these flow into the demons frequenting the **Eastern winds**, who hasten to execute the gracious commands of Grace.

The seventh, **Victory** <note>Original: *Netreth* (Netzach). This emanation represents endurance and triumph.</note>, pours its force into the order of **Principalities**; they emit it to the Archangel **Hanael**, and he finally pours it into the sphere of **Venus**. Her demons (who are subject to that Archangel) then flow into the angels of the lowest order who frequent the **Western winds**.

The eighth is **Praise** <note>Original: *Hod*. In mystical traditions, this represents splendor or majesty.</note>, which commends its will to the order of **Archangels**. They commit the cause to the Archangel **Raphael**, and he again offers it to the demons subject to him who inhabit the sphere of **Mercury**. Finally, pouring it toward the lower realms, they hand it over to the **Mercurial spirits** fluctuating everywhere in the air, inciting winds and rains, so that they may finally fulfill the decree of Praise or of the **Divine Judges** <note>Original: *Elohim*. One of the names of God in the Hebrew Bible, often associated with justice and the natural order.</note>.

The ninth is **Foundation** <note>Original: *Iesod*. Fludd glosses this as "redemption" in the text, though it literally means foundation.</note>, which sends its command downward into the order of **Angels**. This is committed by the Archangel **Gabriel** to the spirits subject to him inhabiting the **Moon**, by whom it is fatally poured to the lower regions and executed by the **Angels of the Northern wind**.

The tenth or last is **Kingdom** <note>Original: *Malchal* (Malkuth). The final Sefirah, representing the physical world and the manifest presence of God.</note>, which transfuses its assigned decree into the sphere of souls. It is commended by the **Soul of the Messiah** to the heavens and the **sublunary elements** <note>The region below the moon, consisting of the four changing elements: Earth, Water, Air, and Fire.</note>, which he commands by the bond of nature. He either binds evil spirits so they cannot bring harm to sublunary creatures, or sets them free for the sake of punishment.

But these things can be best observed if the planets that preside over the winds are rightly understood. For the **Sun** presides over the East, where its intelligence, **Michael**, dominates that part; sometimes **Mars** with his angel **Samael** mixes with him there due to the nature of the place. Furthermore, **Jupiter** and **Venus** preside over the collateral Western winds; hence **Zadkiel** and **Hanael** have power in the winds of that quarter, but the Prince of that place is **Raphael**. Similarly, **Jupiter** and **Mars** look toward the South, no differently than **Venus** and **Saturn** (her opposite) do. Hence **Uriel**, who has the nature of Samael, belongs to the dominion of Jupiter on the western side—namely where the **West Wind** <note>Original: *Zephyrus*.</note> blows.

Similarly, the **Moon** and **Saturn** possess the North; hence **Gabriel**, who is the governor of the Lunar land, and **Zaphkiel**, who is the lord of the Saturnine land, preside over this cardinal point. The governance of **Hanael**, the Angel of Venus, must be in that part where the **Gentle West Wind** <note>Original: *Favonius*.</note> blows and breathes, inclining more toward the North. For **Raphael** (the angel of Mercury) holds the equinoctial point or cardinal direction in the West. Likewise, the dominion of the Angel of the **Moon** is between Western humidity and Northern cold, where the **North-West Wind** <note>Original: *Corus*.</note> blows. The Angel of **Saturn** exerts his force between the dryness of the East and the cold of the North—that is, where the **North Wind** <note>Original: *Boreas* or *Aquilo*.</note> blows, so that the **Arctic Pole** participates in the nature of both; thus that cardinal point produces both snow and hail.

So we also see that the **Antarctic Pole** participates in the nature of **Jupiter** and **Mars**, so that this quarter is partly humid and partly hot. But **Mars** (always approaching the East) is stronger in his nature, while **Jupiter**, turning from the Antarctic toward the Western cardinal point, grows strong gradually in moderate cold. For a greater cold force dominates in the **Moon** in the North, while her humid nature enjoys its freedom more in the South.

From these things it seems clearly declared that God acts through an ordering; the **Angels** who stand before God in the **Empyrean Heaven** <note>The highest, fiery heaven where God and the highest angels dwell.</note> immediately receive these orders according to the same nature promised by that property of God from which the influx comes. Then, through one of those angels, it is commended to the fatal demons of the **ethereal heaven**. Finally, it is committed to the **elemental spirits** (whether benevolent or malevolent) according to the nature of the Name of God and the nature of the predominant planetary angel. From them, it is immediately poured into the sublunary world, and by the breath of this or 그 wind, the pleasure of the **Creator** is led to its conclusion.

Thus, nothing can be found in this world that is not procreated by one of the **Cardinal Angels**. Hence it happened that:

*   By the **Eastern breath**, the element of **Fire** was arranged in the lowest world, and the **Fiery Triplicity** <note>The three zodiac signs associated with fire: Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius.</note> in the Zodiac of the middle world; and **Heat** among the qualities, **Cholera** <note>Yellow bile, one of the four bodily humors.</note> among the humors, **Summer** among the seasons of the year, **Youth** among the ages, animals from the composites, "progressive" animals among the beasts, **Seeds** from the vegetables, **Mars** and the **Sun** among the planets, and **ignited meteors** <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena like lightning or fireballs.</note>, and all things not only composite but also simple that are hot and dry in nature.

*   Similarly, by the **Western wind**, the element of **Air** was ordered in the sublunary world, and the **Aery Triplicity** in the celestial world; and **Humidity** among the qualities, **Blood** among the humors, **Spring** among the seasons, **Adolescence** among the ages, **Plants** from the composites, **Birds** among the animals, **Flowers** from the vegetables, and **benevolent meteors** (such as dew and hoarfrost), and all things both composite and simple that are moderately hot and humid, or temperately cold and humid.

*   After this, by the **Northern spirit**, the element of **Earth** was established in the lowest heaven, and the mass of **Saturn** and the **Moon**, as well as the **Earthy Triplicity** in the middle heaven; and **Coldness** among the qualities, **Melancholy** <note>Black bile, the humor associated with sadness and contemplation.</note> among the humors, **Autumn** among the seasons, and **Decrepit Old Age** among the ages, and **Minerals and Metals** from the composites, **Reptiles** among the animals, **Roots** from the vegetables, and **snow with hail and frost** from the meteors, and all things both composite and simple that are extremely cold and dry.

*   Finally, by the **Southern breath** or wind, the element of **Water** is disposed in the elementary region, and the **Watery Triplicity** in the heaven; and **Aquatic Humidity** from the qualities, **Phlegm** <note>Original: *pituita*. One of the four humors.</note> among the humors, **Winter** among the seasons, **Green Old Age** <note>A term for a vigorous or healthy later life.</note> among the ages, **Stony Minerals** from the composites, **Aquatic creatures** among the animals, **Leaves** from the vegetables, **Clouds** from the watery meteors, and all things both composite and simple that are humid and cold by natu[re]...

...naturally, but accidentally hot. Indeed, the empire of the winds is so vast that it extends even to the underworld. Even the **Phlegethon** <note>In Greek mythology, the river of fire in the underworld; Fludd associates it here with the East.</note>, which is the burning river within them, is infested by the **Eastern wind**; the **Cocytus** <note>The river of wailing.</note> by the **Western wind**; and the **Styx** <note>The river of hatred or "cold" stagnation.</note> by the **Northern wind**—for just as the Phlegethon blazes with fire, so the Styx is stiff with cold—and the **Acheron** <note>The river of woe.</note> is subject to the **Southern wind**. 

Therefore, **Phlegmatic** <note>One of the four humors, associated with water and the South.</note> diseases receive their nourishment or fuel from the South; **Melancholic** <note>Associated with the earth and the North.</note> from the North; **Choleric** <note>Associated with fire and the East.</note> from the East; and mixed diseases arise from the collateral winds (those situated between the Cardinal points) or from contrary winds clashing together to form a single atmospheric disturbance. From this, it is explained clearly enough (as it seems to me) how absurd the opinions of the "Ethnic" <note>Fludd refers to "Ethnici" or pagan/classical physicians like Galen who relied solely on physical explanations.</note> physicians are. They claim the cause of this or that disease is merely phlegm, bile, or melancholy. They lead their disciples—who think only on a superficial level—to believe that if such humors are removed through purging, bloodletting, or sweating, the force of the disease will immediately cease. Thus, they are led into an extreme error. For those of us trained by manifold experience are warned that the disease often grows worse even after the humors are removed. 

The cause is not the humor itself, but the **wind** within that humor, and a spirit, or a malignant light, or an "insane demon" hiding within that wind. These remain even after the phlegm, bile, or melancholy has been purged. The spirit contracts itself into an internally hidden particle and joins with the spirit of the blood, so that it cannot be eradicated without an "occult" <note>Meaning hidden or spiritual, rather than visible/physical.</note> cure. This type of cure is perfected either by using vegetables, animals, or minerals created and constructed in the "opposite blast" (and consequently containing spirits contrary to the author of the disease), or it is completed by the operation of a **Planet** and its **Angel** who opposes the Angel whose subject spirits are harming the sick person. 

The wise men of old were well-versed in this kind of healing, using **sigils**, **characters**, and **incantations** (or words spoken in a fitting manner), by which they attempted to restore the sick to their former health. This can be seen in cases of pestilential diseases, **Epilepsy**, **Paralysis**, **hypochondriacal wind** <note>Flatulence or "vapors" believed to rise from the internal organs to the brain.</note>, and others of this sort, which we shall discuss more copiously in the following second section, God willing. Here, I only wish to warn the reader that Epilepsy should not be treated solely with purges and emetics. Practice teaches us that these are of little or no value, because the nature of the spirit hiding in the body is such that it converts all nourishment into the humor most convenient to it as soon as it gains dominion over the natural spirit of man. We see this also in pestilential fevers and intermittent fevers: though thick phlegm and putrid humor are evacuated today by vomiting or purging, yet tomorrow we find the stomach just as full of putrid humors as if nothing had been removed the day before. Such purging rarely mitigates the disease unless it is at the very beginning, while the malignant spirit introduced through nourishment still remains in the stomach and has not yet been dispersed through the spirit of the blood. At that time, it may happen that by removing the humor of the nourishment in which that spirit or malignant wind hides, it can be ejected from the body with and in the humor (which is its receptacle). But more on this below.

### CHAPTER IV.
#### *Regarding the moist "meteors" <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, mist, and wind.</note> raised by the blast of the Liver (or the microcosmic South), and that the Angel blowing from the South has dominion over it, to direct its blasts toward either health or morbid imbalance.*

The spirit now breathes me toward the Antarctic pole of the **microcosm** <note>The human body.</note>, and turns the blast of my discourse there. Just as that pole is situated opposite the Arctic, so too is it opposed to it in its nature and disposition. Thus, one wind is accustomed to cure and moderate the excesses of the other. For **Boreal** (Northern) winds are said to make the air—disturbed by the **Austral** (Southern) wind—level and clear; and (as **Isidore** <note>Isidore of Seville, a 7th-century scholar.</note> affirms) it opposes the plague that comes from the South. Furthermore, what the North wind freezes, the South wind dissolves; and conversely, what is dissolved by the South is again thickened and hardened by the blast of the North wind. 

To take an example from the poles of the **macrocosm** (the greater world), the **Spleen** <note>Latin: *Lien*.</note> relates to the **Liver** <note>Latin: *Hepar*.</note> as the North pole relates to the South. This is true not only in position but also in quality. For just as the North wind is observed to be cold and dry and to possess an earthy complexion, so too the Spleen is of an earthy nature, being the receptacle of **melancholy**; experience testifies that it emits cold and dry vapors from its region into the microcosm. On the opposite side, the South of the macrocosm is watery and phlegmatic, tending toward heat and moisture; therefore, it emits winds of a similar condition—namely, vaporous ones—which produce perpetual rains when in imbalance. 

Do we not find these same conditions and qualities in the Liver, the place in the microcosm opposite the Spleen? For if the South wind in its imbalance creates damp blasts and disperses them through the world, we sometimes experience rains arising with thunder—specifically when **Mars** has equal dominion with **Jupiter** in that quarter. We see also that if the Liver is affected by a moderate temperament, it produces vapors very similar to clouds. Just as in winter we see dense vapors or mists produced near rivers and ponds, which are later converted into dews and frosts beneficial for the growth of the earth, so we read in the Holy Scriptures: <margin>Genesis 2:6.</margin> *At the beginning of the world, before any rain had fallen on the earth, the whole earth was watered and brought to a convenient fertility,* and this without any man laboring upon it. By the virtue of this same temperament, **Jupiter** is accustomed to water the earth mercifully from the South and refresh it with health-giving moisture, so that the earth may be fruitful. Hence it is said: <margin>Psalms 65:10.</margin> *You have visited the earth* <note>Original Latin quote: *terram visitasti*.</note> *and watered it; you greatly enrich it; the river of God is full of water.* Now, as for what kind of rains these are...

This is what he meant, as if he had said that a fiery, malignant wind or spirit joins most easily with its own kind, and by its burning malignancy destroys the balance of the body’s structure. For bile is nothing other than "fiery air" condensed by a wind like the <term>Eurus</term> <note>The East or Southeast wind.</note>, in which that wind also contains its good hidden spirits, as long as they are kept within the limits of health. But truly, if a burning evil spirit or demon mixes with it, it immediately becomes "furious" <note>Referring to both madness and physical inflammation.</note> and flies straight beyond the borders of health; the body then burns with a <term>Phaeton-like fire</term> <note>A reference to the Greek myth of Phaeton, who lost control of the Sun's chariot and nearly burned the Earth to a cinder.</note> and dries out with decay and blight.

I am able in this place to declare the various effects of the opposing blasts of the winds: namely, the **North** and **South** winds (that is, of the **Spleen** and **Liver**); the **East** and **West** winds (that is, of the **Heart** and the **spermatic vessels**, along with the viscera); the **Eurus** and **Corus** <note>The Southeast and Northwest winds.</note> (or the right side of the upper abdomen and the left spermatic vessels, along with the flanks); and the **North-North-East** and **South-West** winds (that is, the left side of the upper abdomen and the right spermatic vessels along with the colon).
