Job ch. 1.
Clar. maior. 6. 4.
</margin>
Thus, just as the Devil was in that wind of the Macrocosm, or in that air rushing from the region of the desert, by which medium he struck the four corners of the house, which collapsing crushed the children of Job; so also hypochondriac vapors <note>flatus hypochondriaci: internal gases or "winds" thought to cause melancholy or madness</note> are agitated by a malignant spirit and driven with such fury that he may cause the visible temple of man itself to be shaken and sometimes to collapse. Albotali <note>Likely a reference to a medieval Arabic or occult authority</note> seems to affirm this same thing: that melancholy is from a demon, and that every age of the world has seen those affected by demons. The Holy Scriptures also make mention of these; whence we also find that the aerial spirit of the swine, by the permission of Christ, was made a vehicle for <term>Cacodæmons</term> <note>Evil spirits or "bad demons"</note>, by which, being violently agitated by the malignant spirits, those swine were suddenly drowned in the sea. Furthermore, as was said in Job, by the malice of the Devil, fire fell from heaven and consumed the cows, sheep, and boys. In that act, it is certain that the malignant spirit himself was present, namely in the ignited air. So also (as Artesius witnesses), the Devil joins himself to human infirmities arising from Choler <note>One of the four humors, associated with fire and anger</note>, as we shall declare more widely in what follows.

From which it is clearly taught that the human soul, sailing in its lowest spirit, is afflicted through the antipathy of natures by a demon or foreign spirit, and by a genius adverse to the man. Indeed, through the possession of this lowest kind of spirit, man is deceived by false prestiges and delusions, is afflicted by bodily diseases, is driven by fury, imagines false things as true, and is affected by fear and sadness without cause. But observe, I pray, the mystery of this matter, as I gird myself to touch upon it with a needle <note>i.e., to point it out precisely</note>, so that you may more easily understand how God (or the Mind), how one's own soul, and the vital demon (or foreign soul) are said to inhabit the human spirit.

<margin>
Job 2:6.
</margin>
For as the seat of the Mind is the <term>Empyrean spirit</term> <note>The highest, most refined spiritual substance</note>, or the intellectual spirit, in which neither a demon nor a soul of the lowest order can ever dwell; so the proper place for the vital soul is the ethereal spirit, to which the soul is joined as form is to matter. To the first place, on account of its singular purity, the malignant spirit cannot penetrate, as he was banished into dark exile from the throne and presence of God from the beginning of the world, and overwhelmed by darkness for his disobedience. But this spirit or Empyrean air is the seat of the good angels, who are indeed before God. Malignant spirits of this kind cannot even reach the ethereal spirit because, on account of their imperfection and impurity, they cannot approach a place so pure, perfect, and lucid unless God so wills it—insofar as they are called "shunners of light" and "haters of light." And hence it is that they have no power over human life—that is, over his ethereal spirit—without the special permission of God; whence God said to the Devil: *Behold, he is in your hand, but save his soul* <note>original: "animam eius serva" — quoting Job 2:6</note>, that is, do not touch his ethereal part.

Wisdom 7:20.

But truly, noxious spirits or angels who deceive men with delusions are familiar with the sublunary spirit of the world, as this lowest portion of the world—namely the sublunary—was destined for them as a habitation in the beginning after the fall of Lucifer. Hence we find in the Apocalypse: *I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth so that they should not blow upon the earth, nor the sea, nor any tree; and I saw another angel ascending from the rising of the sun, having the seal of the living God, and he cried with a loud voice to the four angels to whom it was given to harm the earth and the sea, saying: Do not harm the earth, nor the sea, nor the trees, until we have marked the servants of God on their foreheads.* By which it is clear that harmful angels have power over the air or winds, over the earth and the sea; but when they proceed to execute their malice, they are accustomed to move through the winds or the aerial spirit. For "spirit" is taken for air and wind, in which the Wise Man <note>Solomon, traditionally the author of the Book of Wisdom</note> seems to recognize the whole force of inferior things to be; whence by John, in the place cited before, angels of this kind are said to preside over the winds.

Similarly, it is evident from the preceding passage that the angels of the higher heavens command those of the sublunary world. For higher things always rule lower things; whence, as the heaven sends its influences into the air and is observed to move it and the spirits enclosed within it, so also the angels rain down their virtues or the force of life from the Empyrean heaven through the <term>Sephirot</term> <note>The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite is revealed</note> into the ethereal heaven, which in turn successively rains those acts into the sublunary world. And God, by a similar reason as the first agent, rains down from his uncreated spirit or lucid fountain all the virtues of the Empyrean heaven, with which the angelic creatures being filled, they are accustomed to pour them liberally from their lucid spheres into the lower ethereal and aerial regions, just as has been sufficiently declared in our <term>Cabalistic physiology</term>.

By these things, therefore, it seems to be declared that it will be very easy for a malignant spirit to penetrate into the air of the microcosm or the subtlety of the blood, since the air and the elements (or sublunary spirit) were destined by God as the natural seat for wicked and harmful demons. Thus, in a delusion of this kind by a foreign demon, the sick sometimes think they see, touch, and taste things which in reality are not there; and sometimes they even believe themselves to fly or swim, when nevertheless it is not in their power either to fly or to swim. Others again believe themselves to have been turned into a donkey or a horse. Others think they ride upon beasts and offer sacrifices or victims to Diana <note>A reference to the "Society of Diana," a common medieval and Renaissance trope for witchcraft delusions</note> while the Moon is shining, and yet meanwhile they are observed to be sleeping securely. Some falsely think they have a fox's tail growing in their anus, others a truly enormous nose, others that they have snakes living in their stomach; and with infinite vanities of this kind, that spirit led without reason deceives the man. And yet the spirit of celestial life is not affected in these people, because the demon is not permitted to touch the soul. But truly, sometimes they do touch the soul by permission, but they are not permitted to totally extinguish it, according to that saying of Augustine: <margin>Book on the Divination of Demons</margin> *Evil angels often receive the power both to send diseases and to render the air morbid by tainting it, and to persuade the perverse to evil deeds:* And elsewhere he says: <margin>Chapter 5</margin> *That it happens by the ineffable power of God that evil angels can do what they do if they are permitted; but they cannot do it precisely because they are not permitted:* <margin>On the Trinity, Book 3</margin> For that spirit, which reigns on its empyrean <note>The highest, most refined heaven of pure light and fire</note> throne in the center of the air of both the macrocosm <note>the universe</note> and the microcosm <note>the human being</note>, either permits demons to approach the aerial margins of the soul itself by contracting into itself, or, by extending itself, puts to flight the light-shunning and wicked demons from the outer soul by the light of its countenance, according to that saying of the Prophet alleged above: *When God hides his face the creatures are troubled; when he sends forth his spirit they are recreated.* <margin>Psalm 104:29</margin> For it was by means <margin>Matthew 12:28</margin> of the lucid spirit of God that *Christ cast out unclean spirits.* Therefore it is necessary that the human soul, swimming in the middle between the divine or empyrean spirit and the mundane or aerial spirit, should adhere to Christ or the Word reigning in the intellectual or highest heaven, if it wishes to be secure from the insults of wicked demons. For if, by neglecting higher things, it tends toward lower or sublunary mundane things—that is, if it fixes its gaze upon the Elements or things composed of elements—it cannot be immune from the tyranny of Devils; indeed, it is very much obnoxious <note>In the Latin sense of "vulnerable" or "subject" to</note> to them. Whence David prayed that <margin>Psalm 143</margin> *God would lead him by his good spirit into the level way*, that is, into the path of truth, which is the spirit of perfection, just as the way of falsehood is that aerial spirit subject to demons; for the Devil is called the *father of lies, John 8:44, because there is no truth in him.* Hence the Archangel says in the *Cabalistic Dogmas*: *Just as all things work together for good for those who love God, so for those who fall away from God, all things cause harm, all things turn toward evil: because the creature arms itself for vengeance against such unruly ones, namely as enemies of God.* Also Augustine says that *the cause of all evils is sin, which is the disorder and distemperament of the soul.* <margin>Augustine, City of God, Book 18</margin> And elsewhere the same Augustine says: *What shall we say of the delusions of demons, except that one must flee from the midst of Babylon? For the more we see the greater power of demons in this lowest realm, the more tenaciously we must adhere to the Mediator, through whom we ascend from the lowest to the highest.* Therefore the actions of demons which are performed in the nobler spirit of both the macrocosm and microcosm are illusory and lying, and deceivers of the sight and human senses, both because they happen in the air, over which the malignant angels of God preside, and because the Devil (who is their father) is a deceiver and a liar from the beginning of the world. Whence it happened that the Egyptian sorcerers or enchanters presented their deceptive miracles and illusory visions to the senses of Pharaoh, seeing as they acted sophistically both in the mundane middle air full of inconstancy, and in that of the soul of Pharaoh and those standing by; so that by their fantasies there seemed to be no difference between their own diabolical miracles and the divine ones of Moses. But truly, when they came to the making and appearance of gnats <margin>Exodus</margin>, they who had previously made frogs and serpents could not fashion gnats, because the greater dominion of the prohibiting God was present through the Holy Spirit, which even the magi confessed, saying: *The finger of God is here.* For they placed the foundations of their art in the sophistical and deceptive air by means of the appearances of demons; but he [Moses] planted the bases of his wisdom and operation in the divine and Empyrean spirit, where no deceptions are found, where truth alone reigns, where all things exist infallibly and permanently, with the good angels assisting. And hence it happens that the impious man is said *to turn his spirit against God*, that is, to alienate it from God, which happens when the soul, more prone to the flesh and the external spirit of the blood than to the mind, subjects itself to the power of demons. Thus also an antipathy was made between the spirits of two people, whence Job spoke in this sense: *My spirit has become a stranger to my wife;* <margin>Job 15</margin> for the soul of Job, adhering firmly to the divine mind, retained its weak spirit within its natural laws and in obedience to God; whence also this spirit was alienated from that of his wife, because her soul, looking at lower things, permitted her spirit to be deceived by the Devil and to become rebellious to the divine mind. Whence there was as great a difference between the spirit of Job and that of his wife as between God and the Devil, which Job also seems to declare directly where he says: *The spirit from my understanding made me respond*, <margin>Job 20:3</margin> that is, the intellectual or Empyrean spirit, by means of divine wisdom: to which indeed his soul was firmly adhering even until the final temptation. For a soul adhering to the aerial spirit does not differ from that of a beast, for it is human to adhere to that spirit from which it was primordially created; but we read in the same author that <margin>Job 33:4</margin> *the spirit of the strong God made man, and it is said by the wise man that Jehovah weighs the spirit of a man*, and elsewhere, *The spirit of Jehovah <margin>Proverbs 16:2</margin> weighs all the ways of man.* And elsewhere, *My spirit shall not remain in man forever;* <margin>Genesis 6:3</margin> by which spirit he understands that which, reigning in the soul of man, administers his life, and is called that Empyrean spirit; for with respect to the lowest or aerial or impure spirit, this indeed seems to differ very little from that of beasts. <margin>Ecclesiastes 3:19</margin> Solomon speaks of this thus: *The spirit of man and of the beast is the same; as the one dies, so dies the other;* For it is the elemental spirit that dies, but truly that celestial and super-celestial spirit is immortal, and is as it were the soul and life of that elemental one, which, when taken away, is said to die.

I shall conclude, therefore, that antipathy—both between diverse things and within the same subject, namely in the airy substance of both the macrocosm <note>the universe</note> and the microcosm <note>the human being</note>—consists in the contrariety and opposition of natures or souls, and especially where a demon or some perverse spirit hostilely attacks the spirit of another. Thus also the gaze of the Catablephas <note>original: "Catablephæ"; a legendary Ethiopian beast, likely a gnu or basilisk-type creature, said to kill with its look</note>, filled with poisonous spirits, is said to kill a man from a distance; that is, its malignant spirit is so contrary to the good spirit of the man that it suddenly penetrates and infects his external spirit expanded in the blood, absorbs his radical moisture <term>radical moisture: the innate life-sustaining fluid of the body</term>, and forces the spirit of life to fly out of the body. And yet, nonetheless, this spirit which is ruinous to man is healthful and favorable to the Catablephas. Such also is the antipathy of nature between the spirits of the wolf and the lamb, the lion and the rooster; just as, conversely, such is the principle of sympathy between the magnet and iron, gold and quicksilver <note>mercury</note>, amber and chaff. Moreover, the leader and first fountain of Sympathy is the Word or the highest Light, which is fiery love and everlasting peace. But the origin of Antipathy is the Devil, who is also called Strife <note>original: "Litigium"</note>. The latter participates in darkness and death, the former in light and eternal life. The former tends toward salvation, just as the latter tends toward destruction and ruin. The latter is the occasion of diseases and disturbances for the creature; the former is the fountain of health, and the author of restoring the sick person to their pristine health.

## CHAPTER XI.

### On the Antipathy between the blood of one person and another. From whence it proceeds.

From those things which have been said in the preceding sections, it is manifest that there is as great a discrepancy between the sympathy and antipathy of things as there is between the consonance and dissonance of harmony; and certainly, if we inspect the matter a little more accurately, we shall perceive that the principle of Antipathy is the same as that of symphonic discord, and likewise for sympathy and concord. Whence it happens that between blood that is well-affected and similar to itself, the best harmony is found. So also between healthy and poisonous blood there is a contrary relationship, and their effects are found to be hostile. For example, that blood in women called menstrual, which is nothing other than a superfluous part of the whole blood mass—if it be retained in the body beyond the proper time and custom, we observe it to be the cause of many ailments and preternatural affections, since it sometimes seems to suffocate the principal parts; it induces cachexia <note>a wasting syndrome</note>, which is followed by dropsy, phrenitis <note>inflammation of the brain or delirium</note>, difficulty breathing, suffocation of the womb, and universal corruption of the blood mass. <margin>Book 10, ch. 12</margin> Indeed, there is such toxicity in the substance of this kind of blood that, as Isidore <note>Isidore of Seville, a 7th-century encyclopedist</note> testifies, growing fruits lose their greenness and power of growth by its mere contact; their natural moisture will be dried up and seem to waste away. Similarly, if herbs are contaminated with it, they immediately lose their vigor, trees cease to bear fruit, and even iron itself infected by it is destroyed by rust, and copper contracts a blackness. As for other animals, dogs eating of it become rabid; indeed, I have heard that if a portion of this blood is given to a man in a drink, it induces leprosy in him. Now, the cause of the malignancy of this blood is a certain malignant spirit procreated in it by excessive retention; for the effects of putrefaction produce wonders, just as we see in flesh which is converted by rot into worms and innumerable tiny animals. But truly, this malignant spirit produced by such putrefaction takes on the nature of a most hostile demon, since it affects women in the suffocation of their wombs no differently than if they had been disturbed by some demon. In a clearly similar way, the seed <note>original: "sperma"</note> behaves in the body of a widow or a virgin, or any other woman, and also in men long abstaining from coitus; for in place of the procreation of its human species, it frequently produces a malignant offspring, most hostile to its parents, which like a demon afflicts both sexes with Epilepsy or the "falling sickness," and is eager to affect the female sex with hysterical passion and suffocation of the womb. And these demons or malignant spirits seem to be lunar, inasmuch as they rejoice to exercise their powers and malices especially at the new moon and full moon, and to treat such miserable people unmercifully. For we see, through diligent observation, that as the seed contributes to the production of the nature of man's essence, so also the substance of menstrual blood seems primarily to lead to the elemental subject of the body and its nutrition; from which it is right to gather that both concur in the generation of man: namely, the seed and its internal [spirit] as the beginning of the external, and the menstrual blood for its vegetation and augmentation into the external substance or mass of the fetus. However, the place of generation of that malignant demon, both in the ill-applied spermatic mass and in that of the menstrual blood, is its sublunary part; because in the celestial part of the seed, no malignant spirit can either be produced or penetrate into that region, except insofar as it pertains to its life. But truly, in menstrual blood there is nothing, or certainly not much, of the "fifth essence" <term>quintessence: the purest, celestial element</term>. Whence it happens that it produces far worse effects than the seed.

As for the antipathy of the blood of different or various persons, that which takes on the nature of a cacodemon <note>an evil spirit</note> is accustomed to infect healthy blood, either at a distance or by contact alone. Those who transfer their contagion at a distance use the air as a medium; and of such a kind is he whose elemental spirit is intoxicated by the seeds of pestilence, smallpox, or consumption <note>original: "Phthisicis"; tuberculosis</note>; but to the pestilential blood, the spirit...

And this seems to be confirmed by this speech of the royal <margin>Psalm 78:49; Psalm 90:7</margin> <note>The text cites Ps. 77 and 89 following the Vulgate numbering.</note> psalmist: *He cast upon them the fierceness of his anger, wrath, and indignation, and trouble, by sending evil angels among them.* And elsewhere he says, *We are consumed by thy anger, and by thy wrath are we troubled.* So also Job, smitten by the Devil *from the sole of his foot unto his crown*, said: <margin>Job 6:4</margin> *The arrows of the Almighty are within me, the poison whereof drinketh up my spirit: the terrors of God do set themselves in array against me.* From which it is clear, that by the arrows of the Almighty, he understands malignant spirits invading under the conduct and command of the Devil or the harming angel (of whom it is spoken in Revelation ch. 7); whence he also calls them the terrors of God set in array. Whence he said, *Their poison drinks up my spirit*, and from this it follows that the spirits which affected Job were fiery; for among all other elements, that of fire is the most sensible, and therefore brings greater pain with it. 

There are, however, malignant spirits in the blood which are so gross and earthy that they cannot contaminate the blood of another at a distance; but truly spirits of this kind are accustomed to pour their poison heavily into healthy blood through contact, such as the poison observed to be in those afflicted with the venereal plague <note>syphilis</note>, and also in both men and women defiled by a virulent gonorrhea; the diseased man is accustomed to heavily affect the healthy woman, or vice versa the diseased woman the healthy man, with discharges, ulcers, and other accidents of that passion, such as the Bubo <note>swelling of the lymph nodes</note>, the scab, decay, inflammation, and burning of urine and others of this kind; likewise the leper rejoices to infect the healthy by contact, which contagion indeed is only to be made by touch alone. And the internal principle of this kind of contagion seems to lie hidden in the external spirit of the blood, since an earthy nature cannot ascend into the sky. Therefore these two kinds of contagions differ, because that which performs its actions at a distance is more fiery and airy. Whence it most easily mixes itself with the air cast between the infector and the infected, and participates in the nature of fiery spirits; but that which strikes only through contact is more earthy with dryness, like leprosy, or watery and heavy, like the venereal plague. Whence it does not so easily disperse itself into the nature of the outer air, and this kind seems to participate in the nature of demons both terrestrial and aquatic; indeed, even some demon or malignant spirit of the nature of the aforesaid elements is the cause of such a disease, as you shall have more fully in the following chapter.

## CHAPTER XII.

->On the antipathetic mystery of the blood, as much the choleric and phlegmatic as the melancholic,<-

Just as four complexions <term>complexions: the four temperaments (sanguine, choleric, phlegmatic, melancholic) resulting from the balance of humors</term> of man are reckoned by physicians and philosophers, so indeed the truly sanguine one is not to be discussed in this place, as it is one in which Antipathy does not dwell; for it continually enjoys a temperament, if not to the exact weight, yet to justice <note>a balanced state</note>. The common physicians and philosophers have placed the complexions and their elements, or the primary qualities of the elements, as the causes either of health, if they be kept within their limits, or of diseases, if they recede from the just limits of their temperaments; and thus they have accepted the body as a thing moved in place of the soul which moves it. For when they say a disease arises from heat, cold, moisture, or dryness, they have here explained nothing but the hot, cold, moist, and dry effect of the agent or mover, but truly they have remained utterly ignorant of the nature of the internal agent. So also, plunging themselves yet deeper into the multitude [of errors], they said the cause of this or 그 disease was either non-natural phlegm <note>original: "pituita"</note>—either glassy or crude, or sweet, or acid, or salty; or Bile <note>original: "Bilem"</note>—either yellow, yolk-like, leek-green, rusty, or woad-blue; or melancholy (which they also call black bile)—either corrosive acid, or arising from burnt phlegm; and thus they make the external element or humor the cause of the disease, but not the internal agent, nor were they ignorant of its furious acts in stupor or pain. And this is the reason why physicians today are so uncertain and ignorant in their cures, since they have respect for the effects rather than the primary cause. But we, looking a little more deeply into the nature of this matter and beyond the grasp of the Pagans and Heathens, recognize first of all, that as God is the primary cause of the life of both the world and its creatures, so also He has a reason for their destruction; and for the punishment of sins, He is accustomed to afflict and punish them with diseases, as the primordial author of both life and death, and in life of both health and of the diseases and perturbations of the living, according to their merits and His pleasure. Which seems to be confirmed from many places of the sacred scriptures, one of which cited above is of this kind: <margin>Psalm 104:29</margin> *The creatures are troubled when God hides his face; when he takes away their spirit they die, and return to their dust; when he sends forth his spirit they are recreated.* <margin>Psalm 90:7</margin> Furthermore it is said, that *by thy anger we are consumed and by thy heat we are troubled.* Likewise in another place it is written, *Blessed...*

His soul shall draw near to corruption, etc.* And elsewhere: *With pestilence and plague Jehovah afflicted the house of Pharaoh, because of Abram’s wife.* And elsewhere: *Lest Jehovah fall upon us with pestilence and the sword.* And elsewhere Jehovah says: *Behold, my hand shall be upon the fields, and upon the horses, and the donkeys, and the camels, and the sheep, and the oxen, and a very grievous pestilence.* And elsewhere: *Jehovah shall make the pestilence cleave to thee, until he has consumed thee; Jehovah shall strike thee with wasting, with a hot and burning plague, and with a parching fever and drought, and with blasting, and with the royal disease <note>original: "morbo regio" - likely jaundice or scrofula, often called the King's Evil</note>, which shall pursue thee until thou perish. He shall strike with the ulcer of Egypt, and with hemorrhoids, and with the scab, and with the itch, from which thou canst not be healed, and also with madness and blindness, and astonishment of heart.* And elsewhere: *Jehovah brings death and restores to life, he sends down to the grave and brings back.* Likewise, Jehovah struck the people of Ashdod with hemorrhoids, etc. Likewise, God struck the men of Beth-shemesh with a great slaughter; and Jeremiah, addressing God, said: *Correct me, O Jehovah, but with judgment; not in thine anger, lest thou bring me to nothing.* And elsewhere: *The hands of Jehovah the Lord were against them for evil.* 

But indeed, it must be known that God works in the punishment of the wicked not immediately, but mediately and originally; for whatever things, whether good or evil, happen to creatures, all those are effected by God’s ordination but not his execution. Just as it belongs to a king or emperor to determine and ordain all things according to his mind and conception, but afterwards those things which are ordained are executed by ministers and subordinates; so also God, the disposer of all things, has his angelic ministers, who according to his will act either well or ill toward creatures, and especially toward men. God, therefore, is said to act according to ordination, while the angels, according to execution, set about performing what was ordained by God. And this we have confirmed in many places, both of the Holy Scriptures and of authors worthy of trust. For in the Royal Psalmist we find this written: **Bless the Lord, all ye his angels, mighty in strength, who do his word, hearkening unto the voice of his speech. Bless the Lord, all ye his hosts, ye ministers of his that do his pleasure.** And elsewhere in the same author we have it thus: **Who makest thy angels spirits <note>original: "ventos" - literally "winds"</note>, and thy ministers a flaming fire**, from which it is right to gather that angels are the ministers and powers of God, who either in the form of winds, or flaming fire, or lightning, do the will of God. For there are seven princes of the angels, according to the testimony of Daniel and Tobit, who stand before God, and are ready to carry out his commands, whether for the consolation of a creature or for punishment. Thus the angel of Jehovah was a help to Moses in his journey through the desert: **Behold (says Jehovah), I send my angel before thee, to keep thee in the way.** Similarly, the angel of Jehovah served Hagar; and was a help to Elijah when he was exhausted by hunger in the desert; furthermore, it is said that the angel of the Lord encamps round about them that fear him, and delivers them. And elsewhere: **There shall no evil befall thee, neither shall any plague come nigh thy dwelling, for he hath given his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways; they shall bear thee up in their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.** 

Furthermore, that angels also act for destruction and punishment may be gathered from these things. First, therefore, we read in the Holy Scriptures that God sent upon them the wrath of his indignation, anger, and trouble, by evil angels. Whence it is clear that God executes anger and indignation through evil angels; and elsewhere: **An evil spirit from God came upon Saul, etc.** Whence it is evident: that an evil angel is a spirit of God, one of his ministers. Similarly, it is said that a lying spirit stood before Jehovah, whom he himself chose, that he might deceive the prophets of lies. The Devil was also God’s instrument by which he afflicted Job with ulcers and pains. God also struck the firstborn of the Egyptians not by himself, but through the mediation of his destroyer. Thus Jehovah sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem, to strike it; and when it was being struck, the Lord beheld and repented of the greatness of the evil, and commanded the angel who was striking: *It is enough, now stay thine hand.* And David, lifting up his eyes, saw the angel standing between heaven and earth, with a drawn sword. Thus Jehovah, sending his angel, cut off every mighty man of valor, and the leader and prince in the camp of the king of the Assyrians. But what, I pray, is clearer than that passage in the Apocalypse, in which we read these things: **I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that they should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree; and I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God, and he cried with a loud voice to the four angels to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea, saying: Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of God in their foreheads.** These things being so, let us hear the opinions of some well-versed in <term>occult philosophy</term> <note>The study of hidden forces in nature, often bridging theology and science</note> concerning this matter, and what they judge regarding the primary causes of diseases: and whether they disagree with the sentiment of the Holy Scriptures or not.

<margin>Psellus on demons.</margin>
Psellus <note>Michael Psellus, an 11th-century Byzantine scholar famous for his classification of demons</note> recognized six kinds of demons, the first of which he called <term>fiery</term>, which he said wanders about the higher air; and this kind, without doubt, mingles with and acts in thunder, lightning, comets, and other meteors, both of the macrocosm and the microcosm. The second is <term>aerial</term>, and demons of this kind wander in the air close to us; they are the patrons of windy meteors, and they live and take delight in the air, agitated in the manner of winds. The third is <term>aquatic</term>, which kind immerse themselves in humors and waters, both marine and fresh; they dwell gladly around lakes and rivers, and indeed in the sea, and they desire to destroy and drown many in the waters. Similarly, they stir up waves and tempests in the sea, and sink ships laden with men to the bottom, overwhelming many with the waves. The fourth is <term>terrestrial</term>, which for the most part stays around the earth and opposes earthly things by many means and engines. The fifth is <term>subterranean</term>, as it lurks under the earth and overflows those who dig wells and metals; it causes chasms in the earth, shakes foundations, and stirs up flame-vomiting winds. The sixth and last kind he makes <term>light-shunning</term> <note>original: "lucifugum"</note>, inscrutable and utterly dark, violently destroying things and animals through cold passions. And he says that all these kinds of elementary demons are so disposed that they both hate the Gods and oppose men...

...is considered. But one thing is worse than another, nor indeed does this assertion of Psellus <note>Michael Psellus, an 11th-century Byzantine philosopher known for his treatise on demonology</note> seem to differ from the sense of the Holy Scriptures; for in the passage of the Apocalypse mentioned above, it is said that four angels standing upon the four corners of the world hold the four winds of the earth so that they should not blow. From this it is clear that these are the governors of the winds, where it is also explained that it is given to them to harm the earth and the sea. Now, the North wind has an earthly nature, most cold and dry, and to this are referred the earthly spirits or demons, and consequently, the Angel presiding over this wind is the leader of these legions, namely the terrestrial, subterranean, and light-shunning demons. The South wind with its prefect has dominion over spirits partly aquatic and partly of a gross aerial sort; the West regards the genus of aerial spirits, as the East does the fiery ones.

To begin, therefore, with the nature of malignant spirits: just as in the higher region of the Macrocosm <note>The universe or "great world"</note> fiery meteors are produced, and sometimes mix with the middle region of the air, producing thunder and lightning within it, so also in the choleric blood of the microcosm <note>The human being or "little world"</note> fiery meteors are generated. Of such a kind are burning and pestilential fevers, and for the most part putrid fevers produced from corrupt bile and phlegm, and even false tertian fevers with a rumbling of winds (which we compare to the thunder and lightning produced in the middle region of the microcosmic air) by reason of a certain malignant spirit inhabiting the region of fire and air. And this seems to be established by the words of Artephius <note>A legendary alchemical figure, often identified with Orpheus or Apollonius of Tyana</note> (a man most profound and well-versed in the mysteries of the philosophers): *There are certain infirmities to which the devil joins himself, namely when a humor departs from its proper temperament and disturbs health itself; and this happens most especially in infirmities arising from cholera <note>Yellow bile, the fiery humor</note>, and the cause of this is because the nature of cholera is hot and dry like fire. Now the substance of the Devil is composed of two things, namely fire and air; therefore his apparent part is air, but his hidden part is fire. Whence it is manifest that in this he is contrary and opposed to human nature, which is of a nature of equality. When, therefore, a sickness happens to the body which is of the nature of Cholera, it is likely that it proceeds from the Devil, inasmuch as his hidden part is fiery and choleric; and for this reason he most easily joins himself through harmony with cholera, and thus increases his dominion over the other humors or elements which concur in the composition of the body and especially of the blood. Whence it happens that by reason of this departure from the natural temperament, and the rebellion of cholera against the laws of nature, the soul departs from the body and is separated from it.* Thus he spoke. From which it is demonstrated clearly enough that it is the opinion of that wise man that the admixture of the Devil or fiery spirit with bilious blood (which is accustomed to happen frequently and easily because of the similarity of their natures) tends to excite fevers of every condition, according to the degree and power of the fiery demon; for as cholera participates in fire and air, so also the fiery nature of the Devil is most easily united to fire, and his aerial nature to air, for like is most aptly associated with like. This, then, is the manner—this, I say, is the reason—that fiery meteors of whatever kind are kindled in the body or blood, and from this it arises that bilious complexions are more afflicted by the presence of such preternatural meteors.

But this is also clearly demonstrated through our experiment concerning the element of fire in the Anatomy of Bread, where we indicated an aptitude in it for the attraction of blackness and darkness and for the reception of the malignant nature of the Devil: and for this cause we proved that elementary fire is the cause of corruption, just as celestial fire is the origin of life and generation.

For the reason for injustice or intemperance is in the external and aerial spirit of the soul which is mortal, and not in the internal and ethereal spirit of the soul, which is eternal. Whence also the wise man says, *The body which is corrupted weighs down the soul, and the earthly habitation presses down the mind that muses upon many things.*

<margin>Psalm 143:7.</margin>
<margin>Job 21:4.</margin>
But in truth, this aerial or animal spirit participates in the body, inasmuch as it is the medium between the soul and the body. It is therefore this spirit which is deluded by the Devil; it is this spirit which suffers his violences, whence David speaks of it thus: *My spirit is consumed, and is like those going down into the pit*; and Job: *My spirit is narrowed, etc.* Indeed, insofar as this spirit is affected by depraved and foreign spirits, it communicates its painful passions both to the body, which truly suffers with it, and to the soul, which is immune to passions; nevertheless, the soul burns so vehemently with love for its prison that it even seems to be sharply afflicted by the pains of the same. The soul, which by itself knows not how to grieve or suffer, dreads destruction though it knows not how to perish, and fears defects, though its divine nature in truth cannot fail.

But let us return to our subject and prove from the holy scriptures that evil angels mix themselves with the blood and inflame it with their fiery disposition. The Psalmist says, *He cast upon them the fierceness of his anger, wrath, and indignation, and trouble, by sending evil angels*, where it is clear that by "anger" he understands a febrile heat, and by "evil angels" the ministers executing his will upon rebellious minds. The aquatic genus, says Psellus, <note>Michael Psellus (c. 1017–1078) was a Byzantine scholar whose work on demonology was highly influential in the Renaissance.</note> by its own property, is accustomed to affect the sanguine spirit of a man in such a way that it excites the "falling sickness" <term>Epilepsy</term> and dementia within him. <margin>1 Samuel 8:11</margin>destructive ends. And as it seems to me, such was the evil spirit from God that invaded Saul, by whose instigation Saul threw his spear, with which he could have pinned David to the wall. Indeed, effects of this kind by demons are best expressed in <term>Hypochondriacs</term> <note>In this period, hypochondria referred to a physical disorder of the "hypochondrium" (the area under the ribs) believed to cause melancholy.</note> and other species of melancholy. Whence Albahati <note>Likely referring to Al-Battani or another medieval Arabic authority translated into Latin.</note> dared to boldly affirm that melancholy is from a demon. Finally, the subterranean and even light-fleeing demons are, in their nature, exceedingly malicious and pernicious; for these not only deprave and hurt the souls of men with evil fantasies and schemes, but also, wandering about in the manner of wild beasts, they hasten to the destruction of men. Furthermore, the aerial spirits do not act upon us through domination, but through delusion: for by their nature they draw near to our elementary spirit (which is the organ and medium of our phantasy), to whom the invisible corporeal mass is "microcosmic air." Whence, just as fiery demons most easily adhere to the spirit of the <term>choleric humor</term> through harmony, so also air joins itself to the natural air by a certain instinct; and this is the cause why demons of this kind affect the spirit in man with various dispositions, tending toward his perturbation as well as toward his pleasures and joy. For if they are urged by depraved influences, such as those of Saturn or Mars, they are affected by sadness, fear, or vexations, or are incited by them to wrath, fury, and brawls; but when Mercury is reigning, they vex them with various "winds" <note>This refers to both spiritual "vapors" and physical flatulence, thought to disturb the mind.</note> according to the nature of the planet to which Mercury’s aspect applies, whom they hold as their chief patron. But conversely, if Mercury looks upon such planets as are good for human life, such as Jupiter and Venus, then they are more favorable to the human spirit, and sound with a certain imperceptible whispering of pleasure, gladness, or carnal joy; for they are accustomed to produce their words and voices with a whisper and sound peculiar only to the one in whose spirit they reside, and imperceptible to any other spirit, since spiritual things are least or only with difficulty subjected to the corporeal senses. But because the voice of such hidden sounds is coupled with the spirit of the soul, the soul itself catches it immediately, just as one is accustomed to catch the voice of another speaking in a whisper while those standing by are unaware.

<margin>Wisdom 9:15</margin>Hence it is, therefore, that a hostile war is waged by demons of this kind, yet we are utterly ignorant of the authors of such contention, which the Wise Man seems to argue with these words: > *For the corruptible body presses down the soul, and the earthly tabernacle weighs down the mind that muses upon many things. We see that if a sword or dagger is moved toward a well-polished concave mirror, the sword or dagger will seem to tend outside the mirror into the eye of the mover by a certain reverberation; indeed, the feigned image of that dagger or arm in the air will be as apparent as if the substance of both were real, and not a likeness, so that I confess at first sight I was struck with trembling fear, by which I was forced to step back suddenly. In a perspective conclusion of this kind, therefore, these four things are found: namely, the object which is truly seen (the dagger); and the eye of the viewer; and the mirror, receiving the false idea of the true thing and emitting it into the aerial medium; and finally the aerial medium, which, receiving into itself the false object created in the mirror, presents it to the eye of the viewer as true. To the eye contiguous to the air, therefore, we compare the sight of the soul of the deceived man, to which the sanguine air immediately enclosing and surrounding it desires to propose its false likeness, fashioned by an aerial demon and imprinted in it as if in a polished mirror; the mirror fashioned from air is the body of the spirit or aerial demon. <meta>This page continues the discussion of how various categories of demons (aerial, aquatic, and terrestrial) manipulate the human spirit and humors, specifically focusing on the "aerial spirit" of the blood as a bridge for these influences and the author's personal experience with fever-induced hallucinations.</meta>

# On the Mystical Anatomy of the Blood

...in those demonic mirrors is the aerial spirit in human blood, by means of which the soul is joined with the body; and this spirit is in itself phantastic <note>In the early modern period, "phantastic" referred to the faculty of the "phantasy" or imagination, which was believed to be a physical process in the brain's ventricles.</note> and, in the manner of celestial mercury, is capable of any impression, however slight, for all the impressions of things are present in the worldly air. Furthermore, because of the close disposition of the nature of demons to that air, the bloody air (which we have elsewhere called the "animal spirit") is suited to receive all impressions similar to itself. Therefore, the spirit in which the soul is immediately carried is accustomed to judge these false impressions—whether of the healthy or the sick, and whether in dreams or in waking states—which is why the soul considers them so true and infallible. Because of that close relationship between the soul and this spirit of its own, the most wicked and stupendous effects are produced, such as experience clearly demonstrates in dementia, delirium, the hypochondriac passion, mania, and other types of melancholy.

Indeed, I confess that I myself, when I was afflicted almost unto death by a pestilential fever, experienced the effects of such malignant spirits. During that time, I was oppressed by perpetual wakefulness for seven or eight days; and whenever I repeatedly attempted to settle myself for sleep, I suddenly and distinctly heard the ringing or tolling of many bells, by which every power of sleeping was always hindered. A forced company of vigils stayed with me through that whole space of time, and even music composed of wind instruments penetrated my ears so precisely from many directions during my waking hours that it was even in my power to transcribe any symphonic part with pen and ink. Furthermore, they represented before my eyes the most foul images of monstrous men, as if they were true and living; and even little men <term>homunculi</term> appeared to me, riding and seriously communicating secret matters among themselves. Had not God, by His grace (to whom immortal thanks are given), maintained a sound mind in me, they would have led me into despair and finally into madness. But I recognized the frauds of these spirits, and I experienced firsthand that their delusions were vain and of no moment or danger, and thus by divine goodness I was restored to my former health. But in this place, I wish to signify to you in passing that where a melancholic vapor <note>original: "flatus melancholicus"</note> joins with a burning fever <term>Causon</term>, there such spirits are usually present with fiery ones; for just as fire and air are united by a sympathy of nature and connected to one another, so also the spirits of both come together and are joined in bonds of peace, as is seen in thunder and lightning, at which time whirlwinds are most frequent.

Finally, as pertains to the demons of the lower spheres—namely the aquatic, terrestrial, subterranean, and light-fleeing—*these (says Marcus Psellus, addressing Marcus)* <note>Michael Psellus (c. 1017–1078) was a Byzantine scholar whose dialogue "De Operatione Daemonum" (On the Operation of Demons) categorized spirits based on the elements.</note> *contrive nothing wisely, nor do they attempt anything by craft or sophistry, because such subtlety is not in them; for which reason they are more foul and base, and more subject to the senses, and consequently they hurt in a more open and visible manner. Yet they act malignantly against human bodies, the reason for which is obvious, since their bodies participate more in water and earth (which are visible elements) than in air and fire (which are invisible elements).*

To begin, therefore, with the aquatic ones: these are accustomed to occupy the spirit of those with pituitous blood or a phlegmatic complexion, and they make the aquatic humor more dominant than the others. And because the bodies of such demons are coarser and more aquatic than those of the aerial ones, as soon as they creep into the aerial spirit (which is the more delicate part of the true blood) in those with pituitous blood, they are accustomed to block and harden the passages between the natural and vital faculties, and even between those and the animal faculties. For they thicken the aerial or animal spirit (which is itself dense and of an aquatic condition) by their presence, because (according to Psellus) the animal spirit is constrained by the thickness of such demonic bodies. From this it happens that the principal powers of the body do not perform their functions or actions, whence motions are slow, stupid, and sometimes completely interrupted; for in this genus is the first degree of cold, which has the property of thickening and congealing humors. Whence these spirits are the chief cause of Epilepsy or the "Comitial disease," <note>original: "morbi Comitialis." In ancient Rome, epilepsy was called the "Comitial disease" because meetings of the citizen assembly (comitia) were cancelled if a participant had a seizure, viewed as an omen.</note> which occurs because of the obstruction of the brain's passages, which is caused by phlegm <note>original: "pituita"</note> condensed by the presence of a malignant spirit. But lest any scrupulous persons mock this opinion of mine, affirming that a demon is the hidden cause of Epilepsy, let us hear Christ himself speaking: <margin>Matthew 17:15</margin> *"Lord (a certain man said to him), have mercy on my son, for he is a lunatic, and suffers greatly; for he often falls into the fire, and frequently into the water." And Christ said, "Bring him to me," which being done, he rebuked him, and the demon went out of him, and the boy was cured from that hour.* The Moon has dominion over spirits of this kind, whence it happens that at the full moon and new moon the possessed are more frequently affected, and also that they yield foam and viscous phlegm. There are also southern spirits who produce catarrhs and defluxions, and even aquatic diseases tending toward heat and saltiness. But in this case, aerial spirits join themselves with these, specifically while Mercury regards the Moon; for just as the regal angel of Mercury is the presiding officer of the aerial spirits—who is a shapeshifter and changes himself according to the nature of the planet to which he applies—so also the prince Gabriel, the angel of the Moon, permits the spirits subject to him in the sublunary world to change and vary their actions according to his planet’s applications.

Now let us approach the terrestrial demons, over whom the angel of Saturn presides; and therefore these are observed to be exceedingly malicious and pernicious, and most opposed to the vital nature. There are three genera of these: the lower of which is worse than the higher, and the worst of all is that of the light-fleeing ones <term>lucifugi</term>. The nature of these is to adhere to the aerial spirit of melancholic blood. The highest genus of these is the terrestrial ones, who are more lively than the rest because they are of earthly things, and therefore they are more watchful than others; they agitate melancholy of the first type, make men fools, and produce many such infirmities according to the applications of Saturn with the other planets. The nature of the subterranean demons, however, is to make men hypochondriacs and maniacs, and these exert their powers most while Saturn is received by Mars, or some ill-fated radiation is made between them. For just as these spirits are accustomed to produce horrible disturbances in the earth—inasmuch as they make gaps in the earth, shake its foundations, and [cause] flame-vomiting...

### Book II. Section I. Portion III. Part III.

...they stir up winds, which from that cause are called <term>Typhons</term> <note>Whirlwinds or violent storms, here used as a metaphor for internal turbulence</note>; so also in the earth of the microcosm <note>the human body</note> they sometimes shake the whole fabric, and are accustomed to produce hypochondriac gases—excited from the center of the Spleen or the microcosmic earth and mixed with fiery heat—whence they excite mania and <term>Lycanthropy</term> <note>A delusional state where a patient believes they have transformed into a wolf</note>. In these diseases, those possessed or suffering use the spirit as if it were their own instrument, and through it they cry out, and sometimes speak in languages not understood by the patient. 

Moreover, the worst of all these kinds is that of the <term>lucifuges</term> <note>original: "lucifugorum," literally "light-shunners," a class of terrestrial or subterranean demons</note>, as they bring sluggishness and torpor to the body, and restrain the voice (*as Marcus taught us*) and render the possessed person as if dead. The reason for this is that this kind is more terrestrial than the others, and consequently excels the others in coldness and dryness; it takes on the nature of Saturn, which is most hostile to the human race. Whence it happens that into whomsoever this kind creeps, it for the most part blunts, dulls, obscures, and destroys their animal power. And such a species of demons is therefore called "deaf and mute" not only by Marcus himself, but also by the sacred scriptures, because men possessed by them are made such, being utterly deprived of their reason. Therefore, we believe these demons to be the cause of Apoplexy, Paralysis, Stupor, Catalepsy, Lethargy, <term>Carus</term> <note>A profound state of stupor or semi-coma</note>, and other such diseases, among which Apoplexy is the worst of all.

May the most kind reader grant me pardon if at first glance these things seem harsh and impossible to him, but truly I would wish him to inquire into the matter with a slightly more accurate sense, and see first of all whether there is any action in a raw humor by itself, or in a mere imbalance of qualities alone, which can inflict such injury and violence upon human nature (which in its balance is most strong)? Namely, in raw phlegm, or in bile heated beyond its nature, we do not find such power by itself that it could so manfully resist nature, or obtain such a victory over the "governors" of human life in four, seven, or more days, or erect and fix the trophies of such great ruin. It is necessary, therefore, that the principle of that preternatural action be internal to the animal or living nature, by which it can blunt and destroy the vigor of the vital soul. 

Since, therefore, the origin of every action is light, which is the principle of heat, just as that is the act, so also God is the source of light. He rains his acts down by means of the human spirit—first into the Angels according to His will, whether for blessing or for punishment, and then from them to the stars of the ethereal heaven by means of angels of the first rank, and then to all sublunary creatures. Whence it is clear that every victory is obtained by the stronger; but the angels have governance over lower things and execute God's ordinances in them, as they are His ministers, ready to perform His will for the creature's good or ill. We should not believe, therefore, that human life can be extinguished by a more ignoble thing, but only by something stronger and more powerful than itself.

But I know many respond that this is the opinion of Hippocrates and Galen, whom we have experienced as truthful up to this time: They teach us that the causes of diseases are hot, cold, moist, or dry imbalances, or the rebellion and overabundance of humors, or their depravity, or a multitude of gases and winds. But I will now boldly say that they did not produce a falsehood in this matter, but it is spoken improperly—just as it is said that a candle illuminates a room, for it is not the candle, but its flame; nor indeed can a <term>bombard</term> <note>An early type of cannon</note> do any evil where there is no powder in which its action resides; nor is a sword properly said to have killed a man, but rather the man as the primary agent. For indeed the ancient physicians looked to the elements, but they either were ignorant of their primary agents, or they did not wish to reveal them to the world, or at least to only a very few. 

We Christians say that if something prosperous or adverse happens to us (even neglecting the external instrument), "God did this to us." Indeed, both in the investigation of the principles of diseases and in the search for the origin of health, one must proceed by descending step by step from God, who is the Being of beings and the Act of acts. One must look to the secondary powers—namely the Angels—and then afterwards descend to the creatures governed by the angels and their influences, and finally proceed to the subjected sensible things, such as qualities, humors, and other such things as passive elements. But let us hear what Psellus says in speaking to Marcus, after he had made mention of the preternatural dispositions of demons in the human spirit: 

*Psellus seems to reply thus: "O Marcus, the followers of physicians lead us to believe some more recent ideas, asserting that passions of this kind are not the effects of demons, but of humors, vapors, and winds behaving badly; and so they are accustomed to attack these with medicines and diet, not with songs or the expiations of incantations." To whom Marcus replies: "It is no wonder that the physicians say this, who know nothing beyond the senses and have dwelled only upon knowing bodies. Perhaps it was fitting for them to think that the sleep-inducing heaviness of the head, the distress of black bile, frenzy, and delusions—which they are accustomed to soothe with baths, potions, evacuations, or plasters—were the inconvenience of bad humors. But as for inspirations and 'occupations' by which the one who is possessed can do nothing—not by intellect, not by reason, not by phantasy, not by sense—it is something else that moves and leads them; and he says, moreover, things which the occupied person did not know, and sometimes predicts future things; in what way (I ask) shall we say these are the erratic motions of matter?"* These are his words.

And in truth, I myself have known many laboring under a burning fever, some of whom, with a preceding delirium, divined the day and hour of their death. And a certain man laboring under the plague understood through a vision that he would soon die, and it seemed to him that after his death he himself contended with another as to who should first enter through a certain narrow way; and in this contention of his, two men of honorable gravity arrived, to whose judgment this controversy was recommended, and thus the privilege of entering first was granted to him. When this sick man died a few days later and was led to the grave, a contention arose between his friends and those of another dead person over the grave; and so at last the dispute was settled by two elders of the parish of St. Andrew, and the grave was awarded to the one who had dreamed. Alzarabius <note>Likely Al-Zahrawi (Albucasis), a famous medieval physician</note> also confirms this opinion of Marcus in the place cited before...

### On the Mystical Anatomy of the Blood.

...it seems, where he asserts that diseases invade men both through transgressions and through cursed demons, whom they were accustomed to cure through ancient sciences now hidden from men; for by their subtlety <note>their fine, ethereal nature</note> they mingle themselves with human blood, corrupting the entire humoral mass, as appears from the most savage plague inflicted on Job by the Devil, where no human remedies were of use; thus he says. But if it still remains in the mass of the blood, that bloodletting usually brings no benefit or relief. Furthermore, let us also hear Augustine speaking on this matter. <margin>The City of God, book 21.</margin> Truly, what is written in Ecclesiasticus chapter 4: *A heavy yoke is upon the sons of Adam from the day of their coming out of their mother's womb, until the day of their burial into the mother of all* <note>meaning the earth</note>, *must be fulfilled to such an extent that even little ones—though now released through the washing of regeneration from the bond of original sin by which alone they were held—suffering many things, undergo some attacks by malignant spirits.* And Jerome, concerning the death of Blesilla in his letter to Paula <note>original: "Paulum," likely a transcription error for Paula</note>, says: *What is the reason that those sucking at the mother's breasts are corrupted by a demon?* He also speaks clearly and brightly of aerial spirits and of their subtle way of operating within us in the Decree placed in chapter *Sciendum* 36, question 4. Where, after he had spoken some words concerning their excellence over men and other creatures because of their subtle and aerial composition, he continues thus: *They often receive power both to send diseases, and to make the air itself sickly by tainting it, and to persuade the perverse and lovers of earthly comforts to evil deeds: persuading in wonderful and invisible ways by penetrating the bodies of men without them feeling it through that subtlety, and by mixing themselves into their thoughts through certain imaginary commands, whether of those awake or sleeping.* <margin>Augustine, On the Divination of Demons.</margin> And elsewhere he says: <margin>On Matthew, book 1.</margin> *They often receive power both to send diseases, and to make the air sickly by tainting it, and to persuade the perverse to evil deeds.* Similarly, John Chrysostom says, *The Devil does not tempt men as much as he wishes, because as far as he is concerned, he would never cease from temptation; for he has no other action—he does not eat, nor sleep, nor perform anything else, except to tempt, deceive, and subvert: this is his food.* Finally, from the Apocalypse in the place cited above, we gather that power and permission are granted to demons to harm the earth and men, and to subvert the air and the waters. Whence I think it can be hidden from no wise man that all diseases proceed from those four angels to whose power the governance of the winds is committed. And this even the Pagan physicians perceived by diligent observation through a "demonstration from the posterior"—that is, from the effect—and not "from the prior" <note>from the underlying cause</note>, as those who were unable to penetrate to the internal agent of the disease. Hence says Hippocrates: <margin>Aphorisms, book 3, 1.</margin> *Changes of the seasons especially produce diseases, and in certain seasons great changes of either cold or heat.*

Here he himself saw that changes of the seasons in heat and cold are the cause of diseases, but he was ignorant that either fiery or earthly angels are the principles of these alterations, acting in the winds; therefore they placed the effect for the efficient cause. And elsewhere: <margin>Aphorisms, book 3, 4.</margin> *In seasons when on the same day there is now heat, now cold, one should expect autumnal diseases.*

For by the conflict of demons of contrary conditions, the seeds of contention are left in the air, which, entering into bodies through inhalation or nourishment, produce false and putrid fevers through hidden opposition; for which reason they <note>the Pagan doctors</note> placed the causes as corrupted <term>pituita</term> <note>phlegm</note> or "suffering phlegm" and acting <term>bile</term>. And elsewhere: <margin>Aphorisms, book 3, 7.</margin> <margin>Aphorisms, 3, 11.</margin> *In droughts, acute fevers occur. And if the year has been for the most part such as the constitution it has made, such diseases for the most part should be expected. And elsewhere: Concerning the seasons, if indeed the winter has been dry and Northerly, but the spring rainy and Southerly, it is necessary in summer to have acute fevers and inflammations of the eyes* <note>original: "lippitudines"</note>, *and difficulties of the intestines, etc.*

Here, however, he makes the winds the causes of these diseases; and yet he was ignorant of the Angels who are the procreators of the winds, of whom mention is made in the Apocalypse. And so that whole book makes mention everywhere of diseases proceeding from the blasts of the winds and various constitutions of the air. By which it is evident that if the Angels who have the power either to restrain or to release the winds are malignant and harmful to both the earth and its creatures, by means of the blasts of the winds—under which are subjected infinite legions of harmful ministers, who, obeying their command, mingle themselves with the winds and disperse themselves everywhere in the air, polluting and contaminating it with their poisonous blasts, and with it also desire to penetrate the secret places of the human heart by divine permission, and thus transform a healthy disposition into a diseased one; if, I say, those angels have the power of disturbing and changing the air with their instruments from better to worse, and also sometimes by divine compulsion from worse to better, it would have been better for these Pagan physicians to have searched into the secret natures of those angels and the manner of loosening those knots—as they are the primary agents in diseases—than to vainly torture the elements and humors themselves like blind men; just as if some madman (having no regard for the fire that acts or burns) should wish to beat the fire with a whip or strike it with a sword or axe because it has been turned into a flame, thinking that by this path he would take away the harm or damage of the fire; when, however, the violence of the fire is in no way hindered by this, and it nonetheless continues in its action. By similar reasoning, physicians name and regard sensible passive things, but they are ignorant of and neglect the internal active essences. Hence, therefore, for the most part they purge in vain, they let blood in vain, they administer altering potions in vain, so that they observe more die under their hands and endure the extreme suffering than return to the limits of their former health by the virtue of common medicine. And if some are reduced to their former state, for the most part the vigor of nature itself—which is able to endure the examination of the expected <term>crisis</term> <note>the turning point of a disease</note>—brought more benefit than the power of the medicine itself; and this indeed happens because the hidden properties of herbs and animals, to which it is given to expel this or that demon and suppress its malignancy in the body, are hidden from the common sort.

# SECTION I. PORTION III. PART III.

## CHAPTER I.

*In which it is proven that the spermatic vessels correspond to the fourth quarter of the Western sky. Similarly, various opinions on the origin of sperm and seed are explained.*

---

<image-desc>A large, square decorative initial 'A' featuring intricate woodcut engravings of scrolling foliage, leaves, and a central human face or mask integrated into the letter's design.</image-desc>

At last, we turn the point of our needle or stylus—touched by the soul's magnetic desire—toward the Western point, and it comes to mind to offer a few, yet sufficiently clear, words concerning the setting of the microcosmic sun. Just as in the first part of the preceding sections we mentioned the northern and southern poles of the <term>microcosm<note>The "little world"; the human body viewed as a miniature reflection of the universe.</note></term>, and then in the second part spoke of its bloody air in general along with its mysteries; so now we shall approach its western angle or hinge. For just as we shall describe the human origin or "Eastern region" below in the secrets of the heart, so in this place we compare the seminal vessels to the point of the West. Thus, the sperm or seed contained within them is compared to the setting Sun, and those hidden viscera to the earth.

For what else, I ask, is the seed but the <term>quintessence<note>The "fifth essence" or purest, most concentrated spiritual component of a substance.</note></term> of life, descending from the place of the sun (the heart) where it arises in the microcosm, into these vessels? The seed contained in them is like the sun descending or setting, prepared for the uterine "sepulcher" in which it dies—or at least appears to be changed—until it rises again and produces a new creature, similar to the first. Likewise, the setting Sun appears to us to die and lose its life or light, and the night (which is likened to corruption) follows, until the sun rises again in the East as before. In exactly the same way, the seed—which is the Sun of life and generation—which previously rose in the heart to illuminate the human life and "earth," now sets in the seminal vessels. There, descending into the womb, it seems to die, and yet it lives secretly and acts continually to produce a new creature, in whose heart it seems to rise to illuminate its own earth, no differently than the <term>macrocosmic sun<note>The physical sun in the outer universe or "great world."</note></term> does for its own.

But since this cannot be well considered by the common people, because it is extremely difficult to investigate and explain the hidden generation of seed—so uncertain is the opinion of almost all philosophers and even physicians regarding it, being so unstable and inconsistent in their judgments—I have thought it worthwhile to first explain some of their opinions, along with certain arguments against them, and then afterward I will explain my own view. Though my view is new and (as far as I know) unheard of until this day, I will prove it to be certain and to be received without any controversy through the clear evidence of untarnished truth.

<note>original: *Albertus Magnus in mulierum secretis*</note> Albert the Great, in *The Secrets of Women*, says that sperm is nothing other than the "superfluity of nourishment" which recedes into a substance not intended for feeding the body. He was indeed a man most prudent in philosophy, yet in this definition he is (as it seems to me) not at all accurate and is inconsistent with himself. He dared to assign the origin of something so divine—such as the seed, in which so many gifts of the heavens and such great vigor of spirits lie hidden—to the "excess of food." Thus, he unwisely believes that that vile thing (which cannot be reduced into the nature of blood) is converted into precious sperm, whose soul is the seed—as if the entire power of the fetus, its living soul, and its specific virtue consisted of the waste from food and drink! There are also others who are more demented in their judgment of procreation, and they want it to be made from the very substance of the brain. If this were indeed likely, it would follow that those who engage in much sexual intercourse would have very little brain left...

...of the brain; furthermore, it is clear that this assertion is by no means consistent, because the proportions of the entire body and the paternal signs impressed upon all the members of the father or mother cannot originate solely from the brain. Finally, who is so weak in philosophical speculation as to be ignorant that the vital and natural spirits differ in location and nature from those <term>animal spirits<note>In early modern physiology, "animal spirits" were not "spirits of animals," but the most refined fluids of the body responsible for thought and sensation, centered in the brain.</note></term> (which abound in the brain)? Yet since like tends to be procreated by like, he who is generated from sperm gushing from the brain alone would undoubtedly not be a "man of heart" (as they say), but would be purely intellectual, being born and forged entirely from cerebral substance. 

Others (*among whom I name Galen, in his booklet—or at least the one attributed to him—"On Sperm"*), affirm that sperm descends from every humor of the body which is made from the subtler nature of the four <term>humors<note>The four bodily fluids: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.</note></term>. Indeed, these thinkers seem to denote only the visible body or mass of the sperm; they have not even considered its heavenly soul or the internal and invisible part which we call the <term>seed<note>The author distinguishes between "sperm" (the visible material) and "seed" (the invisible, spiritual spark of life within it).</note></term>, since in this passage they seem to speak only of sublunary humors. 

Others well-versed in philosophy recognize an internal acting cause in the sperm, which they confess to be a certain quality and <term>occult force<note>A "hidden" or non-obvious power.</note></term> implanted in the seed by nature, which they say arises from the principal parts of the body. They claim this force informs the matter of living bodies with a similar form and species (*for I have read Velcurio<note>Johannes Velcurio (1490–1559), a commentator on Aristotle and physics.</note>, among others, alleging this*). By this confession, <note>original: "ignotum per ignotius"</note> "the unknown is explained by the even more unknown," for who is so foolish as not to know that the "form" in every thing is that internal agent by which the external is driven and moved, or that it is a certain hidden and formal thing which attributes a specific essence to a visible creature? Furthermore, these men fall into the same absurdity as the others, wishing that a "specific form" (which is of heavenly substance) could be derived from parts of the body (which are elemental or forged from the elements).

*Aristotle also among the philosophers, and Fernel among the physicians,* declare sperm with a more cautious and broader definition, saying that *it is the seed from which those things that are constituted according to nature first arise.* These men, therefore, define it by its effect, and not by its essence. 

But we, indeed, with a clearer method and a slightly more elevated style, shall explain not only the origin of the sperm but also of the seed lurking within it—both heavenly and elementary—along with the reason for their mutual mixing and preparation. We shall demonstrate that it is nothing other than an airy spirit driven from all the breaths of the parts of the <term>microcosm<note>The human body viewed as a "little world" mirroring the universe.</note></term> into the form of a microcosmic cloud by the power of the spirit or heavenly wind (which also has its own <term>daemon<note>Here meaning a guiding spirit or internal genius, not an evil "demon."</note></term> or bright internal genius, moving it by the instinct of God presiding over it). And we shall show that it is composed of an elementary part regarding the external, and a heavenly part regarding the internal.

<margin>Ezekiel 37:5</margin>
So it is also said in Ezekiel: *The Lord said, "Behold, I will send spirit into you, and you shall live, and I will place sinews upon you, and will cause flesh to grow over you, and will stretch skin over you, and I will give you spirit and you shall live." And (says the Lord) "Breathe from the four winds upon these slain, that they may come to life," and the spirit entered into them and they lived again.* 

From these words it is evident that sperm itself is a cloud or air naturally collected and condensed from all the "winds" of the body, the internal part of which is an angel appointed by God who holds the protection of life. Indeed, three angels concur in the being of the sperm: one is the intellectual wind or spirit, which has power over the animal spirit emitted from the empyrean heaven; the second is the ethereal breath, which presides over the vital spirit; and the last is the elementary wind or spirit, having power over the natural faculty. Hence, three bubbles are usually seen in the sperm after it has remained in the womb for six days.

### Chapter II.

#### *That sperm is composed of two things, and that it is contracted by a spirit or wind in the natural body into the form of a cloud; and concerning the manner of the generation of sperm.*

As it is certain and known to all that man is composed of body and soul, so it is by no means hidden from the skilled that sperm is forged from two things: namely, the external and visible, which is drawn from the purer substance of the elements (and in this place takes the role of the body and is properly called "sperm"), and the internal or invisible, which descends from heaven by means of the air, concerning which we shall speak below.

But before we speak of the origin of these humors rooted in the generation of the parts, and the manner of their joining, it is necessary first that we consider the four "preparing vessels" of the sperm. Two of these descend on each side toward the testicles—namely, a vein and an artery. On the left side, from the left emulgent vein, another descends; specifically an artery or <term>aorta</term>, or "great artery," proceeding near the left kidney, it likewise tends downward. Also on the right side, one vessel—namely, a vein—stretches downward from the trunk of the <term>vena cava</term>, but the artery emerges from the same place of the aortic trunk as the left one, and likewise inclines toward the testicles in the manner of the left. 

It should be known, however, that each vessel of each side is forged from a vein and an artery (as has been said); in its descent toward the testes, it weaves and entwines itself by a wonderful union or plexus in the form of a silken web. The Greeks call this texture <term>Anastomesin<note>Anastomosis: a connection or opening between two things that are normally diverging or branching, such as blood vessels.</note></term>. This sort of entanglement of vein and artery lasts from about the middle of the descent all the way to the testicles themselves; these we have frequently called the "expurgating vessels" in common anatomy. These things having been rightly considered, we shall proceed to what follows.
