# Robert Fludd’s Reply

From this kind of arrangement of the monochord, we see that its division according to the laws of Geometry agrees in all respects with the intention of Plato. And although his harmonic proportions are explained by numbers through the method of Arithmetic, and mine are drawn upon a flat surface using compasses according to the method of geometry, I do not see what could prevent them from corresponding to each other. Indeed, the proportions of both arts agree in the same way, just as the connection between <term>Cossic numbers</term> <note>Early algebraic notation, from the Italian 'cosa' (thing).</note> and Algebraic numbers is very clearly described. Therefore, just as a unit exceeding the number eight is a <term>sesquioctave</term> <note>A ratio of 9:8, which defines a whole musical tone.</note> proportion and is the measure of a tone between two extremes: so we divide this Monochord into 9 parts, and a single part is the interval of the first tone in this monochord—that is, the 9:8 proportion of the whole—and this space of the monochord relates to the interval between 384 and 432.

Next, we divide the distance of the Monochord between Jupiter ♃ and Saturn ℏ into another 9 equal parts. The first part will be the 9:8 proportion to that distance, and consequently, it corresponds to the value of one tone. Therefore, the second tone in the monochord is this space, D. E., which stands in the same state as the Platonic proportion of 432 and 486. After that, we divide the whole Monochord into four equal parts, and where the previous one ends—namely at F—there will be the end of the minor semitone or <term>limma</term> <note>original: *lemma*; a small Pythagorean semitone.</note>. Thus, the space between E and F is that interval of the monochord called the Limma. But since the fourth part of the monochord is in the <term>sesquitertial</term> <note>A ratio of 4:3, defining a Perfect Fourth.</note> proportion (namely 3 and its third part, which is 4), a **Perfect Fourth** <note>original: *Diatessaron*</note> is produced here from two tones, D-E and E-F, and the Semitone E-F. This space E-F in the monochord is to this monochord as 486 is to 512 in the Platonic or <term>Proclean</term> <note>Refers to the philosopher Proclus.</note> Heptachord.

We have, therefore, produced here the consonance of an imperfect **Perfect Fourth**. We shall proceed to find the remaining intervals, and we divide the space between F and Jupiter ♃ again into 9 equal parts, the first 9:8 part of which—namely between F and G—will be the value of one tone, which in the monochord corresponds to the interval of the numbers 512 and 576. This is the distance or difference between the lesser middle-point 512 and the greater 576. Then another tone is tracked down by clearly the same reasoning: the interval between G and Jupiter ♃ is divided into nine equal parts, and the space G-A will be the second tone from the semitone, which stands as the interval between 576 and 648.

After this, the third tone from the previous Semitone is drawn out by the same reasoning, by dividing A-Saturn ℏ into nine equal parts. The interval of this tone will be a-b, and it stands as 648 and 729. Finally, the <term>sesquialter</term> <note>A ratio of 3:2, defining a Perfect Fifth.</note> part of the Monochord between F (where the Fourth ends) and Saturn ℏ (or the double proportion, but half of the whole monochord C-Saturn ℏ) will be the part at c. The boundary of the interval b-c is a limma, and the point C is the boundary of the **Perfect Fifth** <note>original: *Diapente*</note> concluded between F and c, which indeed consists of three tones with a semitone. Or, it is the boundary of the **Octave** <note>original: *Diapason*</note>, counting from C, which is composed of a Fifth and a Fourth. For the discovery of the other intervals—namely c-d, d-e, e-f, f-g, g-aa, aa-bb, and bb-cc, and so on for the rest—one must either proceed to investigate the tones by dividing c-Saturn ℏ into 9 equal parts, and produce the first semitone e-f by dividing c-Jupiter ♃ into 4 equal parts, and that last portion of the monochord bb-cc by dividing c-Saturn ℏ into three equal parts. Or, all of this is completed more quickly by proceeding from any letter toward Saturn ℏ, always dividing the whole into two equal parts. For example: If I wish to find the true place of d, then I divide D-Jupiter ♃ into two equal parts, and the middle intersection will be d; similarly, the middle intersection of the space E-Saturn ℏ will be e; and so on for the others. But since this division of our Monochord agrees in all proportions—both extreme and intermediate, and consequently in harmonic consonances—with the Platonic Heptachord as corrected by Proclus and filled with the smallest intervals, let us now see, I pray, whether its parts and proportions can be rightly and fitly compared to the Harmony of the Macrocosm, or not. 

The Sages have called God the center and the circumference, as He who is all that is, yet He is said to surpass all things in Himself and to be outside all things—that is, infinite and incomprehensible. For this reason, <term>Hermes Trismegistus</term> <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure linked to alchemy and philosophy.</note> also made a circle (speaking metaphorically) whose center is everywhere, but whose circumference is nowhere. And hence Job says (Chapter 11, verse 9), as has been frequently cited, that the wisdom of God is not to be found, since "it is higher than the highest heavens, and deeper than the lowest grave, its measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea." God was therefore in Himself alone—that is, in the center—before creation; but from the center He progressed to the periphery in creation, revealing Himself to the formless waters. Whence it is written: "The Spirit of the Lord moved over the waters," and (as some add) with a circular motion, imparting a fiery vigor to them. But the medium by which God the Father extended Himself from the center to the periphery, where the Spirit of the Lord moved, was the Word; and all these things are but one and the same essence with the Word. Just as the center and the diameter, with its parts and the periphery, differ not at all from the essence of the circle, nor are they distinguished from each other. Therefore, just as all intervals between the center and the periphery are filled by the semi-diameter, so every spirit of the world between its center and circumference is informed and perfected by the Word; nor is a vacuum found any longer in the nature of things, according to that saying of Saint Peter (2 Peter 3): "The heavens were of old, and the Earth consisting of Water and through water by the Word of God." And Saint John (Chapter 1): "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning with God. All things were made through him, and without him was nothing made that was made." From this, then, comes the true explanation of the world's Harmony through the metaphorical Circle. But let us return to the matter.

# In the Defense against the 12th Analysis

The method of demonstration, although commonly thought to be *a priori* <note>original: "à priori"; reasoning from cause to effect.</note>—since God is said to be in the "heaven of heavens," that is, in the outer boundary of the world according to common understanding—is nevertheless truly a demonstration *a posteriori* <note>original: "à posteriori"; reasoning from observed effects back to the cause.</note>. Just as every center must be considered before its surrounding circle, so too was God in His own center and in Himself before He shone forth and revealed Himself out of the darkness at the creation of the world. Therefore, for the sake of the common intellect (which considers all things as they now appear to the eyes), I produced my *Physics* and its *Harmony* by proceeding step-by-step from God's seat, situated or imagined at the circumference or summit of the world. However, it is well-known and explained among the Wise that God is everywhere; and we find in the Holy Scriptures that God fills the world with His presence and power, which does not differ from His essence. And in that same place, we find that the holy spirit of discipline fills the whole orb of the earth. Thus it was said (as before) in **Job 11**: *The Wisdom of God is higher than the highest heavens, deeper than the lowest grave, its measure longer than the earth, and wider than the sea.* From this, one argues that Wisdom is in all the intervals between the world's periphery and its center, and yet, in respect to herself, she is outside of all things.

Therefore, God is said to be in the "heaven of heavens" insofar as it is the most worthy place—whether He is in the earth, in elemental bodies, or in the celestial ones—and also in the more worthy and more lucid spirit of the elements themselves, called the "fiery" or "empyrean" <note>The Empyrean was the highest part of the heavens in ancient cosmology, believed to be composed of pure fire or light.</note> because of its excellence. This spirit is found everywhere, just as God is said to be everywhere; for He chose that primary created Light as His primary garment in this world. The intellectual eyes of the Apostle [Paul] penetrated even to that garment when he said he was caught up into the "third heaven," where he relates seeing marvelous and ineffable things. For, as we have said, just as the Empyrean or Angelic heaven is taken for the third heaven or the heaven of heavens, so too if this heaven is God’s throne, it is necessary that wherever God is, there also is this heaven. But God, as has been said, is essentially present everywhere; therefore, that heaven is also everywhere: namely, in the Sun (as God's tabernacle), in the thick cloud (as His hut), in the earth (which was granted to bring forth the Savior), in Man (as the temple of God), and in every creature (insofar as life is in the Word). Thus, the "highest heaven" is understood in terms of the highest dignity, purity, and exaltation. In the same way, we say a Bishop is "exalted" in dignity, not in physical size.

Regarding the demonstration and revelation of God, speaking in a mystical and non-vulgar manner, we think it is *a priori* from the center rather than the circumference. For no one of sound mind would say that a circumference is prior to its center in time or order. Hence it is said that God appeared out of the darkness at the creation of the world. And **Hermes Trismegistus** <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure associated with the origins of alchemy, magic, and philosophy.</note> said that *the Monad generated a Monad and reflected its own heat back into itself.* The Holy Scriptures also acknowledge that in creation, God appeared out of darkness; and again, that "Darkness was His secret place." Because of this, God is called by the **Cabalists** <note>Followers of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah), whose ideas Fludd integrated into his Christian philosophy.</note> the "Hidden God" (*Deus latens*), insofar as He is considered in Himself or His center, and also the "Dark Aleph" <note>Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing unity or God.</note>. But by emitting His rays circularly from His point or from Himself, even unto infinity, He brings potential waters into action; and thus the world was created. Hence He is called by the Cabalists the "Bright Aleph" and the "Revealed God" (*Deus patens*), which is that divine wisdom that flowed out and emanated from the bosom of the Father before all created things (as found in **Ecclesiasticus 1**), following that saying of Hermes Trismegistus quoted above: *The Monad generates a Monad, etc.*

Therefore, from the earth or the heart of darkness (since it is said to bring forth the Savior) as a center of the mundane circle more manifest to us, we extend our "mundane monochord" toward its periphery (and indeed beyond all things). Thus, we have placed that "Lesser Aleph" of the Cabalists, signifying unity, in the center—that is, at the first end of the monochord or semidiameter—which is marked on the monochord by the letter **C**. The "Great Aleph," the character for the number one thousand, signifies multitude at the circumference, following that arrangement of the Platonic Enneads (999) or the ordering of the letters of **Jehovah** [יהוה], where:
*   **Iod** [י] is the center, **c**.
*   The first **He** [ה] is the interval from **a** to **c**.
*   **Vau** [ו] is explained by **e**, indicating the internal nature of the Sun.
*   And the final **He** [ה] is the last progress of God into multitude, by which He returns again to Himself—namely to the **Iod**, from which the first outflow began. 

Because of this, these letters are observed by the Cabalists to be the only ones among all Hebrew letters that are spherical and round. We see, therefore, that between *Iod* and *Vau*—specifically through *He* or the pure spirit—the spiritual **Diapason** <note>An octave, the most perfect musical interval.</note> harmony is found, as it emanates immediately from the *Iod* out of darkness at the creation of the world. From this, Light and the Empyrean heaven were created on the first day, and the ethereal heaven on the second, with the Spirit of the Lord—the *Vau* or **Metatron** <note>An archangel in mystical Judaism often associated with the voice of God or the celestial scribe.</note>—moving over the waters in place of the Sun. Then, between *Vau* and *Iod* again—namely through the space of *He* or the coarse elemental spirit—another harmony of the *Diapason* (the material one) is constituted. Through this harmonic connection, material things pass from the circumference (or God) into spiritual things, and those finally into God Himself, who is the center. Thus *Iod*, *He*, and *Vau* fill all the intervals of the mundane monochord.

But perhaps you will say all these things are merely mystical and Cabalistic; let us therefore proceed by a way more open and clear to your eyes. You see that a string of a monochord, stretched equally, is but one single thing, and it produces one certain and immobile sound when struck. But if it is pressed directly in the middle—namely at **n**, **C**, and **c**—it gives the same and equal sounds (that is, of the same tone); and yet the portion of the string **c-C** compared to the whole string **C-n** will, when struck, give the first *Diapason* harmony. Likewise, the portion **c-n** struck with the whole will give the second, a double proportion similar in all respects to the first, except that this one is more immersed in multitude, having been further dilated from the source **c**. Thus, in this ocular experiment, we have "One" before any dimension—namely, we consider the string by itself alone and in its whole self. From **a**, **c** to **n**, we also have "Two"—namely, two portions of the string, sounding a double *Diapason* harmony with the whole or the unity of the string. Here we see a notable progression of the Trinity from Unity in the same proportion or most perfect harmony, according to the pattern of which...

### Robert Fludd’s Reply

Every harmony of number, whether binary <note>relating to the number two</note> or ternary <note>relating to the number three</note>, is expressed in the world. For from one string, two sections are made; likewise the Son, who is not divided from the Father in essence, emanated from the one Father. Thus, the Monad <note>the number one; unity</note> generates the Monad, and 1 becomes 2. From this, the first **Octave** <note>term: Diapason; the most perfect musical interval, representing a 2:1 ratio</note> was produced in the world, and 2 returns again into unity. (For just as the Monad generated the Monad, so it reflected its own heat back into itself). In this way, the number 3 was produced, which is the idea or pattern of the Office of the Trinity within the unity of essence. For we have but a single string, yet in this one string we have three properties of the most perfect Harmony, which complete the universal harmony of the world: for where the **Octave** is present, the **Fifth** <note>term: Diapente; a musical interval with a 3:2 ratio</note> and the **Fourth** <note>term: Diatessaron; a musical interval with a 4:3 ratio</note> are likewise necessarily included.

The Monad (1) generates the Monad (1), and they are II in the place of the sun, or the heart of the world—which is why it is called the "sphere of equality"—and it reflected its heat back into the 1, and they are III, which are nothing but the single Monad. This is seen in the name *Iod* in *Vau* through *He*, and *Vau* again in *Iod* through *He* in the great name of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH</note>, or the "small Aleph" progressing into the "large Aleph." From this, one argues that all things are in one and through one, and consequently, that multitude is nothing but unity. In this manner, the worldly circle is filled and perfected in every direction by its harmonic semi-diameters—both the middle and the extremes—counting from its center to the periphery.

But if you seek even more manifest proofs of this matter, know that all perfection comes from God, the highest source of perfection. He relates to the **monochord** <note>a single-stringed instrument used to illustrate mathematical proportions in music</note> insofar as He extends from the center to the circumference. Hence, God is called the center, the circumference, and the point of perfection. He produces this perfection in the world by means of His presence in the middle of the world’s diameter; from that midpoint toward God—both as He is the circumference and as He is the center—there is a correspondence to unity in a "double proportion" <note>a 2:1 ratio</note>. This produces the most perfect consonance, and therefore the fullest expression of the luminous Deity, because every "more-than-perfection" resides in God.

Let us proceed, then, and apply our discourse to the Sun, which is indeed the most splendid, most lucid, and most perfect of all creatures, holding the same place in the world as gold does among metals. It follows, therefore, that just as the measure of the **Octave**—or the most perfect consonance—coincides in the midpoint of the monochord between the two extremes (the center and circumference), so also this midpoint in the world exists in the solar center as the place of highest perfection among created things. Consequently, the position of the sun is directly in the heart between God-the-center and God-the-circumference. The soul of the sun on earth, pouring out its harmony and the lesser consonances of the world-spirit, is from God, in God, and through God. Indeed, God Himself—no less than the soul sounding the entire string—is the same in the whole and in every part of it. This is the very thing the Prophet seems to acknowledge when he asserts that *God placed His Tabernacle in the sun* <note>original: "Deum posuisse Tabernaculum suum in sole"; a reference to Psalm 19:4</note>.

However, I would like it to become known to you in passing, **Johannes** <note>Johannes Kepler, Fludd’s primary intellectual rival</note>, that although I may seem to take away all power from the stars as mere "creatures" in my *Analytical Declaration*, I nevertheless attribute all power to God the Creator operating within them. I make Him the fountain and origin of Harmony here, and the Sun His instrument and, as it were, the receptacle for the rays of His perfection. Consequently, generally speaking, the Sun is the location of the **Octave** in this world. Thus we see a burning mirror, receiving the rays of the sun (which are not themselves on fire), produces a more evident and violent effect than the sun does by its own power alone. I say, therefore, that the Spirit of Wisdom is poured everywhere into the world and gives life to man and other creatures, as well as to the Sun; yet God uses the Sun as an instrument to produce more rapid changes in both generation and decay within denser spirits. But I always attribute all these things to the Creator—to the Wisdom expanded everywhere throughout the world and operating in a secret way—and not to the creature. 

Thus, I would say there are not only two suns in the world, but infinite suns; in every single thing of the world, there is a "Sun of Wisdom," far clearer and more brilliant than the visible sun, providing life, motion, and being to every thing, however small. Hence Democritus and Orpheus said that *all things are full of gods*, but they attributed all these gods to a single Jupiter—that is, to uncreated Wisdom. And when they said this, Johannes, they were not stiff from a hangover, nor distended with German wine, nor intoxicated by the fumes of British beer, as you seem to suggest so "kindly" regarding me on page 46. For I want you to know that the "double proportion" or the harmony of the **Octave**—that is, of perfection—exists in the smallest creature just as in the largest, namely the world. This is demonstrated from that very monochord. For the double proportion of CCCCC to ccccc (which denotes the mineral kingdom among compound things) possesses a Harmony just as complete as the double proportion of C to c, which denotes the harmonic proportion between God-the-center and the sphere of equality, or the Sun. For the craftsman will find all things in a compound creature that are found in the visible world; indeed, he can even proceed further with his refinements. From this it is clear that uncreated Wisdom, or the Sun, is in every creature, since the consonance of "more-than-perfection" is found therein. But it shines forth more in one than in another—both in the World and in man, and in man more than others. This, I say, is brilliantly explained by the degrees of the divisions of the monochord into double proportions.

Here, therefore, you see the two extremes of general Harmony, which are nothing but the same thing and meet in one; for otherwise there would be no return from God into God. Here you also see the midpoint of the universal worldly Harmony, which creates peace and concord between the life of the creature (both of the heavens and the earth) and the Creator Himself: namely, the uncreated soul, which placed its Tabernacle in the sun. And this soul is that highest Wisdom, the Messiah and the Word, of whom the Apostle Paul speaks, clearly arguing (as was said before) that not only men but all other things are led to their true Harmonies through the blood of Christ. His words are these:
> Making peace through the blood of his cross for all things, both those on earth and those in the heavens. <note>original: "Pacificans per sanguinem suæ crucis res omnes, quæ sunt in terra, & illas quæ sunt in cœlis"; Colossians 1:20</note>

### In Defense of Analysis XII

From these things, therefore, it is clearly evident that the string of the monochord in its entirety refers to the Father, who, as He is unity, is also everything that exists, filling all His things with harmony. But in dividing Himself according to His justice into equal parts, He reveals the emanation of unity into duality <note>the movement from one into two</note>—namely, that which is the image of the Second Person <note>the Son</note>, who fashions the world and its parts according to harmonic proportions. 

The second portion of unity, emanating from the center of the string **c.** (or the first portion) just as the Son proceeds from the Father—namely, the space from **c.** to **$\gamma$.**—is related to the Holy Spirit. This is that property which joins the spherical point **c.** with the capital **C.** in a union of love and harmony, giving life and power to all creatures of the world. This is according to that saying of the royal Psalmist: *By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and by the breath of his mouth all their power.* <note>original: "Verbo Domini firmati sunt coeli, & Spiritu ab ore eius omnis virtus eorum" (Psalm 33:6)</note> It is as if he were saying that by the emanation of the perfect consonance of the **Octave** <note>term: Diapason; the 2:1 harmonic ratio</note>—that is, the shining Word—the heavens were made firm, emitting light from the central **C.** (the Father) to the mundane **c.**; and by the emanation of the **Octave** consonance (the space **c. $\gamma$.**) emanating from both, the world is completed and its creatures are given form.

But because the Sun in this world is endowed with the most ample divinity (insofar as it is most full of Light, according to St. Augustine and others who say: *The more light something has in itself, the more it seems to claim God for itself* <note>original: "Quantum magis aliquid lucis in se habet, tantum magis Dei sibi vendicare videtur"</note>; and that saying of Plato and Apuleius: *Do not speak of God without Light* <note>original: "Ne loquaris de Deo sine Lumine"</note>, as He is the father of light), it therefore participates most greatly in the harmonic perfection of God. Consequently, its proportion to God is as **C.** to **c.**—namely, a double proportion <note>2:1 ratio</note>, which produces the most perfect consonance of the **Octave**. Because of its most perfect aspect toward Him, Wisdom (which is the highest perfection of all things leaping forth from the fountain of perfection) is said to have placed her tabernacle in the Sun. 

Here, then, we have the **Alpha** as the beginning and the **Omega** as the end. In the midpoint between them is established the most beautiful of all creatures <note>the Sun</note>, being more fit and worthy because of the most polished and pure substance of its body to receive the rays of highest perfection from both extremes of the circular perfection, joined and continued with one another through a union of inexplicable love.

We see, therefore, from the diligent mystery of this Monochord, how God is the center and how He is the circumference: namely, the center hidden within Himself before creation, and the circumference in and after creation through the revelation and expansion of His rays in a circuit—and finally, the whole in the whole, or everything that is, insofar as it is a circle. For just as the string (which they compare to the semi-diameter of a circle) fills all the intervals of the monochord, so also God, manifesting Himself circularly in creation or rising peripherally from the heart of darkness, is said to fill the mundane spirit or the "waters" with the splendor of the Word (who is likewise God). This follows the saying of Saint Peter: *From water, in water, and through water the heaven and earth were made by means of the Word.* <note>original: "Ex aqua, in aqua, & per aquam coelum & terra sunt facta mediante Verbo" (paraphrase of 2 Peter 3:5)</note> 

We also see by what proportion of perfection God migrated into the Sun after creation: namely, by a leap of a double proportion <note>the 2:1 octave</note>. From this it is clear that the Sun must be in the very middle between God as the center and God as the circumference. And this place where the Sun walks is called by the Platonists the **sphere of equality**, as if they were saying: in this place, the semi-diameter is equally divided into a double and equal proportion from both ends—namely, from God the center and God the circumference—constituting a double **Octave**. 

But where does Johannes <note>Johannes Kepler, Fludd’s primary intellectual rival</note> find an error here among these three principal terms of the general World Harmony? Or where in these proportions is there found so grave a "sin" as he seems to claim in his 26th text? Or is this demonstration of mine shrouded in the most perplexed riddles and mysteries? Does this not seem to agree with the opinions of both the Philosophers and the Holy Scriptures? Does not the judgment and reason of any man of sound mind confirm this? Indeed, if the reader prepares himself to consider and contemplate this with due respect, he will observe that the matter truly cannot be otherwise.

But Johannes will perhaps ask: how can the remaining intervals of the world be filled if only these three terms are admitted? I answer that where a major consonance—namely, the **Octave**—is found, there the minor consonances are also necessarily understood to be present. And where these minor ones are imprinted on the monochord of the world, there also the smallest intervals are included: namely, the whole tone and the semitones. 

Furthermore, we can fill these minor intervals of the monochord in this way: by starting from the dissolution of the composite and moving backward via the path of generation, proceeding from Alpha to Omega. We do this by counting the orders of the heavens as they are commonly accepted—that is, in the quantitative distance and position of place—even though in truth the harmonic progression of God in nature happens according to degrees of depuration and purification, through which the subtle becomes step-by-step, and the corruptible becomes incorruptible. This is according to the Apostle: *What is sown corporeal and corruptible, will rise spiritual and incorruptible.* <note>original: "Quod seminatur corporeum & corruptibile, surget spirituale & incorruptibile" (1 Corinthians 15:42-44)</note> 

The space between **C.** and **D.**, therefore, relates to that between the Earth and the Air—namely, Water—corresponding to a **tone**. And again, between **D.** and **E.** to that interval between Water and Fire—namely, Air—assigning another **tone**. And between **E.** and **F.** to that between Air and the Moon—namely, Fire—which corresponds to a **semitone** because of its sharpness and thinness. And such intervals in the sublunary heaven are found among themselves in a **sesquialtera** proportion <note>a 3:2 ratio</note>, from which an imperfect consonance—the **Fourth** <note>term: Diatessaron; a 4:3 ratio</note>—arises. The nature of this Fourth best suits this region of the world, as it is imperfect, being subject to generation, corruption, and change. 

We proceed now to the intervals of the middle region of the world, or the ethereal heaven, and we say that the space between **F.** and **G.** relates to the sphere of the Moon between Fire and that of Mercury, and it corresponds to a single **tone**. And that between **G.** and **a.** is as the sphere of Mercury between that of the Moon and Venus, related to another **tone**. And that between **a.** and **b.** is as the sphere of Venus placed between Mercury and the Sun, compared to a third **tone**. And **b.** to **c.** is as the sphere of the Sun between that of Venus and Mars, responding to the condition of a **semitone**...

### Robert Fludd’s Reply

...because of the subtle, pure, fiery, and hidden virtue of the solar nature; and thus the material **<term>Fifth</term> <note>original: Diapente; a musical interval where the frequency ratio is 3:2</note>** is produced, which is a consonance of lesser perfection. For such is the nature of the heaven, to which the **Quintessence** <note>The "fifth element," a pure celestial substance distinct from earth, water, air, and fire</note> most rightly seems to belong because of this consonance. And from these two lesser consonances, the material **<term>Octave</term> <note>original: Diapason; the most perfect consonance, a 2:1 ratio</note>** was born. But now I would wish John <note>Johannes Kepler, Fludd’s intellectual rival</note> to believe that I have regarded the dignity of these places in their purification and refinement more than in their physical dimensions.

Next, we shall proceed in the same way from God in the circumference—or the heaven of heavens—to complete the spiritual **Octave** in the sun in this manner: by dividing the second half of the monochord string into parts similar to the first. I say that the interval between the notes **C. c.** and **b** behaves like the first Hierarchy of Angels <note>The highest rank: Seraphim, Cherubim, and Thrones</note> situated between the seat of God and the region of the second Hierarchy. Because of its infinite purity and subtlety, this space corresponds to a semitone. The interval between **b.** and **a.** behaves like the middle Hierarchy <note>Dominions, Virtues, and Powers</note>, responding to a whole tone. And the interval **a.** to **g.** relates to the lowest Hierarchy <note>Principalities, Archangels, and Angels</note>, referring to a second tone. In this way, we have the spiritual **<term>Fourth</term> <note>original: Diatessaron; a 4:3 ratio</note>**.

Next, the interval **g.** to **f.** behaves like the Eighth Sphere <note>The firmament of fixed stars</note>, compared to a semitone; **f.** to **e.** relates to the sphere of Saturn as a whole tone; **e.** to **d.** corresponds to the sphere of Jupiter as another tone; and finally, **d.** to **c.** relates to the sphere of Mars, which is adjacent to the Sun. Thus, we have the spiritual **Fifth** produced even in the middle heaven. When these are joined together, the greatest and most perfect consonance, the **Octave**, is produced. 

However, if we wish to fulfill these intervals in a mystical and not a common way, then we must proceed in a direction opposite to this. For God, shining forth from the center in the first creation, fulfilled the spiritual **Octave** first, beginning with the creation of the spheres and the worthier creatures, as demonstrated on our Monochord. In this way, the division of the World Monochord into two consonances was completed. And although this John <note>Kepler</note> has attempted to attack this division because of the difference in the dimensions of the heavens, I reply to him here as I do elsewhere: that a thick thing does not differ in "philosophical weight" from an expanded thing. Consequently, units are not measured by lines, but by weights. Therefore, I advise readers to note here that they should not understand my "substances" as being distinguished by physical dimensions of quantity, but by formal quality. 

Consider if the same thing, in the same substance and degree of quantity, was once raw, but is now rendered more mature, pure, transparent, subtle, and incorruptible by the predominance of a shining form within it. From this, that same thing on earth can be led back—through natural purification—from the nature of earth into heaven, and from heaven into the nature of the Spirit of God which encompasses all. In the middle degree of this perfection, the Sun reveals itself, responding to either extreme through the consonance of the **Octave**. 

For example: empty Earth, darkness, and something like "nothingness" is changed by the appearance of light into water; then, by the continuous action of Divine Light, that water is led back into air through purification; and afterward, through a third degree, that air rises into elemental fire by the operation of the Word; and that fire into ether through a fifth degree. Then that purifying light gathers itself into the substance of the Sun, according to that saying of Hippocrates, the divine Philosopher and Physician: *That immortal thing which is called heat, when all things were in confusion, departed into the highest periphery, which the Ancients called ether.* 

And Hermes Trismegistus <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure associated with hermetic philosophy</note> says in his *Sacred Sermon*: *There was an infinite shadow in the abyss, and water besides, and a thin intellectual spirit existed in the chaos through divine power. When all things were indistinct, the light things afterward flew up into the high region, while the heavy things settled under the moist sand. Once things were distinguished and balanced, being carried by the fiery spirit, the heaven shone forth in seven circles.* 

In this way and for this reason, the wise carefully observed the degrees of World Harmony, through which—by the ladder of truth—we ascend from earth to heaven, all the way to the solar body, through the material **Octave**; and then afterward from the Sun to the seat of the Creator Himself through the degrees of the other **Octave**, which is therefore called spiritual. And this is that Jacob’s Ladder, through which the Patriarch dreamed—truly and not as a fiction—of Angels descending from heaven to earth, and ascending from earth back to heaven. 

Furthermore, we have arranged this World Harmony according to Plato’s three "Enneads" <note>Groups of nine</note> (999), dividing the monochord into three **Octave** consonances, as is explained clearly enough in the aforementioned example. To each great consonance, nine stations are attributed with nine voices, which correspond to the **Fifth** and the **Fourth** (from which the **Octave** is composed), just as was explained in my *History of the Macrocosm and Microcosm*.

Furthermore, every region of the world can also be referred to the harmony of the whole. Thus, in my *Macrocosmic Music*, I divided the elementary region of the world (in the manner of the whole) into a double **Octave**, where I made the Sun of the lower world God Himself, *carried in a cloud upon the wings of the winds*, as is held by the royal Psalmist. Indeed, we placed the middle region of the air as the midpoint between the earth and the concave surface of the Moon. 

For this is certain and approved: that a thing which is composed of the elements of the world—and which possesses within itself, according to its proportion to the whole, the most exact degrees of World Harmony—is proven to be a "Son of the World." This is found in Man <note>the Microcosm</note>, and in that "precious clay" from which Adam was first extracted, which we call the true Microcosm, and which has been experienced very often by the sons of the true Art of Physics <note>likely referring to Alchemists/Hermeticists</note>.

But now, just as we divided the entire World Monochord into two equal parts—a double **Octave** consonance sounding to its whole—which was the closest example to the Divine Idea in the Archetypal World; so also we now divide it into three parts according to the example of the "Second Idea" which exists in the created world. We divide these parts unequally because of the inequality of the worldly regions in the arrangement of thick or subtle matter with form. # In the Defense against the Annals, Book 12.

...regarded with respect to the properties of the Trinity working within it. Therefore, according to the exemplar of both the **<term>Macrocosm</term> <note>The "Great World" or the universe itself</note>** and the **<term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "Little World," meaning Man</note>** (which is the image of Wisdom shining before all things into the darkness of the world), God created both the world and Man. Hence, **<note>original: *Mercur. Trismegistus*</note> Hermes Trismegistus** called Man the "son of the World," just as he called the World the "son of God." For just as the world is divided into the **Empyrean heaven**, the **ethereal spirit**, and the **elemental region**, so too is Man composed of the **divine mind**, the **living spirit**, and the **opaque body**. In exactly the same way, Moses divided the **Ark** or **Tabernacle** into three parts: the portion called the **Holy of Holies**, where the Cherubim were; the middle region adorned with gold and seven lamps; and the part subject to the sky and changes of the air, destined for the slaughter and death of cattle. So also was **Solomon’s Temple** distinguished into three parts, each excelling the other in dignity, following the exemplar of Moses’s Tabernacle. Therefore, **Wisdom** (or the Word) is the image of the Father; the **World** is the image of Wisdom; **Man** is the image of the world; the **Tabernacle of Moses** is the image of Man; and finally, the **Temple of Solomon** is the likeness of the Tabernacle.

Therefore, through the emanation of Wisdom from the Father, the perfection of the **First Harmony** is achieved through the consonance of the **<term>Octave</term> <note>original: Diapason; the interval of a 2:1 ratio, representing perfect spiritual resonance</note>** in this world. This occurs through another Octave in the unity of essence—which flows from the Father as the source or center, and Wisdom as the Son and the bright river of life (or the diameter filling the circle and establishing a "tabernacle in the sun"). The **Third Person** <note>The Holy Spirit</note> of the same essence joins these two extremes into one by an inviolable bond. So also in the great name, the **<term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God: YHWH (יהוה)</note>**, the letter **<term>Iod</term> <note>י (Y)</note>** passes through **<term>He</term> <note>ה (H)</note>** into **<term>Vau</term> <note>ו (W)</note>**, and again through the second **He**, the **Vau** returns back into the **Iod** from which it proceeded. Here, **He** is the sign of the spirit or breath; it is that amatory and everlasting glue by which and through which the Second Person goes out from the First and returns to the First. 

In the same way, in the fabric of the world, **Wisdom** went out from the bosom of the Father—from the dark **<term>Aleph</term> <note>The first Hebrew letter א, here representing the hidden, unmanifest God</note>**, or the "Hidden God," or His unity or center—and immersed itself into the multitude of the world. In the **Spiritual Sun** (that is, in the bright spirit created on the first day), Wisdom placed the tabernacle of its perfection through the first Octave of the world. Because of its subtlety and purity, this space was the most capacious of all. Likewise, the interval of this Octave consonance, leaping immediately from the center **C.** to the note **c.**, is the most capacious of all. In the Divine Idea or the "Great Name," this refers to the first **He**, into which the **Iod** (or Light) immerses itself. In the world, it refers to the **Empyrean heaven** (the fiery, super-celestial, intellectual, and angelic world), which is divided into nine grades of Angels. These are compared to units or "roots" because of their simplicity; these grades represent the first series of **<term>Enneads</term> <note>Groups of nine; a reference to the Neoplatonic ordering of reality</note>** containing nine units. This is the work of the first day of creation. In Man, the **Mind** with its nine dimensions is compared to this region; in the Tabernacle of Moses, the **Holy of Holies**; and in the Temple of Solomon, the secret part guarding the Ark of God.

Next, through the middle Octave, the second region of the World was completed: the **Firmament**, or the starry heaven, or the ether, or the celestial region, following the exemplar of the supreme heaven. For just as **Iod** (the source of Light) first entered **He** (the source of the clearest spirit) for the creation of the Empyrean heaven—that is, the rays of divine light formerly hidden were now diffused through the purer worldly spirit, and by this means **Light**, the first creature, was created—so also the rays of **Iod** itself, immersing themselves deeper through the Empyrean spirit into the worldly and thicker spirit, produced a spirit in the world related to the **Son** in the Trinity (just as that Angelic spirit relates to the Father). From this comes that saying of the Royal Prophet <note>King David, in the Psalms</note> previously cited: *By the Word of the Lord the heavens were established...* This Heaven is denoted in the Tetragrammaton by the letter **Vau**, which is the middle between the first **He** (spirit) and the second **He**, acting like a firmament separating the waters from the waters. 

And here, a less perfect consonance, the **<term>Fifth</term> <note>original: Diapente; a 3:2 ratio</note>**, terminates in the **Sun**, where the Word "placed its Tabernacle"; and the **<term>Fourth</term> <note>original: Diatessaron; a 4:3 ratio</note>**, an even less perfect consonance, ends in the **Moon**, thereby denoting the imperfection of the Moon compared to the Sun. Both the Fifth and the Fourth together constitute the middle **Octave of Life**. This spirit is denser and thicker than the first, and the former informed spirit serves this one, as the soul serves the body. It is divided into nine spheres, which stand in the place of **<term>squares</term> <note>In Fludd's mathematical mysticism, "roots" are more spiritual/simple, while "squares" are more material/complex</note>** to the Angelic "roots," reflecting their relationship of thinness to the ether. In Man, we compare the **Vital Spirit** to this heaven; in the Tabernacle of Moses, the gilded part where there are seven lamps (the icons of the seven Planets); and in the Temple of Solomon, its "heart" or middle part and its mysteries.

Finally, God, descending even deeper into the multitude toward the periphery of things, produced the **material and elemental Octave** of the world. This was the work of the third day, in which the letter of the Tetragrammaton, **Vau**, immersed itself into the final spirit **He**—into the lower waters of the world situated beneath the firmament—just as the letter **Iod** immersed itself into the first **He** (the upper waters). This heaven is attributed to the **Holy Spirit**, as it derived its soul from the first and second heavens, as if from the Father and Son; and it is said of this spirit that "it breathes where it wills." Properly, the "soul" of this heaven is the substance of the middle heaven, just as the soul of the middle is a portion of the upper heaven. Thus, the **Ether** is the body and the **Empyrean** is its soul; the **Air** is the body and the **Ether** is its soul; and the matrix or final receptacle of all these is the **Earth**. 

This lowest region is therefore related to the upper ones as **cubes** are to **roots**. It is signified by the final Ennead of Plato, as it is also divided into nine regions, as I have explained elsewhere in both my **<term>Macrocosmic History</term>** and especially my **<term>Microcosmic History</term>**. In Man, the **body** is compared to this; in the Tabernacle, the part subject to external changes and alterations; and in the Temple of Solomon, the more common and vulgar part. 

Here, however, we think it must be especially observed that on the **<term>monochord</term> <note>A single-stringed instrument used to demonstrate musical ratios</note>**, the quantity of any Octave consonance always becomes more contracted and shorter as one descends. From this, we argue that the matter of any region is thicker and denser, and consequently requires less space for its existence in the world. Thus, we see that a handful of earth, when expanded by refinement into water, requires ten times as much space in its watery nature as it did before in its earthy nature.

# Robert Fludd’s Reply

As for those lower harmonies of the **<term>Octave</term> <note>original: *Diapason*</note>** that arise beyond the general ones, they indeed argue for the existence of composite bodies in which the same Harmony sounds. However, the first and highest rank is assigned to **Man**, specifically between the notes *c c c* and *c c c c*. In Man, the complete harmony of the world is found, counting from Unity (or God) down to the lowest of the Elements, for through Man all things in heaven and on earth are to be saved. Here, Man designates God as the **Alpha and Omega** <note>The first and last letters of the Greek alphabet</note>, or the **Small and Large Aleph** <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, signifying the beginning and the end</note>; he is said to have union with God through God. He is the truest "son of the world," just as the World is the offspring of God.

A second **<term>Octave</term>** is given to the composition of other **animals**. A third is given to **vegetables**, and the last to **minerals**, as they are adjacent to the center of the whole universe. Thus, all things created in the world—counting from Unity up to the number one thousand—are explained most clearly on our **<term>monochord</term> <note>A single-stringed instrument used by ancient and Renaissance theorists to illustrate mathematical proportions in music</note>** according to the intention of **Plato**. 

It is as if composite bodies are cubes made of other cubes. For just as in the simple structure of the world there was a relationship of the "Root" (the supreme heaven) to the "Square" (the ethereal region) and the "Square" to the "Cube" (the elemental heaven), so it is in composite things: 
*   **Animals** relate to **vegetables** as a **Root** relates to a **Square**.
*   **Vegetables** relate to **minerals** as a **Square** relates to a **Cube**. 

Furthermore, **Angelic** (or super-celestial) bodies relate to the **stellar** bodies as a **line** relates to a **surface**, and these relate to **sublunary** <note>Earthly, or "below the moon"</note> bodies as a **surface** relates to a **solid body**. 

We conclude, therefore, that God, existing as One in Himself, is nevertheless all that is. He encompasses all Harmony by His divine power. By the harmony of His perfection, He measured out the supreme heaven; according to that exemplar, the middle heaven was formed on the second day; and finally, the lowest heaven on the third day. Among composite things, **animals** look toward the first heaven, being of a more fiery nature; the head of these is **Man**, who is compared to the **Seraphim** <note>The highest rank of angels</note> who always stand before the face of God. **Vegetables** refer to the middle heaven, as they are more airy; and their head, **Wheat**, is rightly compared to the celestial Sun. **Minerals** are compared to the lowest heaven, as they participate more in gross water; and their head, **Gold**, participates in the central Sun.

I could have published a massive volume on this subject, but it is not my intention to bring weariness to the reader in this little treatise. I only wish to remind him, honestly and candidly, that my "World Harmony" is not so far removed from mathematical proportions as **Johannes <note>Johannes Kepler</note>**—who was deceived in his comparison—imagined. Nor is Robert so ignorant of Platonic, Pythagorean, and Proclean harmony as Kepler has attempted to trumpet to the world.

And now, because it seems to some that Johannes has judged Robert’s knowledge of the Harmony arising from the **five regular solids** <note>The Platonic solids: tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, and icosahedron</note> in an uncivil and light manner—as if I had never sown seeds in this harmonic field, or at least not well—I will show the reader in a few words what I observed in my youth (contrary to Johannes’s opinion) and how much profit I elicited from them. 

Regarding the **regular solids**, we have observed that their five shapes correspond to the parts of the world—namely the heavens and the four elements—according to the opinion of the best mathematicians. We recognize that three of them are formed from triangular surfaces, the fourth from squares, and the fifth from plane pentagons. For mathematicians find no more than these figures in Geometry, because no solid angle can equal or exceed four right angles, as is found more fully in the 21st proposition of the 11th book of **Euclid’s *Elements***.

Therefore, the triangles that meet to form a solid angle must be either three, four, or five. In an equilateral triangle, any angle contains 60 degrees. It follows that three angles of this condition make 180 degrees (which is less than four right angles, or 360 degrees). Consequently, four angles of this kind produce 240 degrees, and five produce 300 degrees. Beyond this, one cannot go with these angles, because six such angles produce 360 degrees, which equals four right angles—a condition that does not fit the nature of a solid angle.

From the meeting of these angles, three figures are produced. The first of these is the **Tetrahedron**, which is clearly a pyramid with four triangular bases. This is likened to the element of **Fire**. Its solid angle consists of three plane angles or surfaces of a triangle with equal sides, as appears in the following illustration.

# Robert Fludd’s Reply

...to one right angle and a third part of a right angle: wherefore, since three angles of a hexagonal figure are equivalent to four right angles <note>In a flat plane, three 120-degree angles of a hexagon meet to form 360 degrees, which equals four 90-degree right angles. Because they lay flat, they cannot "fold" to form the corner of a three-dimensional shape</note>, they cannot be admitted into a **solid angle**. From these facts, therefore, it appears certain that there are only five figures of regular bodies described by us, and no more.

Regarding the **Harmony** or the proportion of these figures to the parts of the world, the **Platonists** <note>Followers of Plato, who in his dialogue *Timaeus* associated the regular solids with the elements</note> establish the following: namely, that the **Cube**, being the most stable and firm among all figures, corresponds to the **Earth**, which is fixed and immobile. Furthermore, they applied the **Pyramid** (or **Tetrahedron**) to the element of **Fire**, as fire is observed to reach upward in such a shape. Truly, since the **Octahedron** closely approaches the composition and figure of the pyramid, they assigned to it the Element of **Air**, as air is closest to fire. Next, they adapted the **Icosahedron** to **Water** (because it has many different sides and angles), for water, due to the diversity of its waves, is changed into infinite forms like **Proteus** <note>A Greek sea-god capable of changing his shape at will</note>. And finally, they compare and liken the **Dodecahedron** to the **Heaven** (since it allows for the inscription of all other figures within itself), because heaven, by its natural embrace, contains all things. Moreover, this figure is most perfectly adapted to the heaven in this way: just as the heaven is most conveniently divided into 360 parts or degrees, so too is the Dodecahedron observed to consist of just as many right angles. For this figure consists of twenty solid angles, and three pentagons meet to form each of them; in every pentagon, three equilateral triangles are found <note>Fludd is using a symbolic geometric breakdown here to reach his numerological total</note>, so that in every solid angle there are nine equilateral triangles, which, multiplied by 20, make 180. In every triangle, three [angles] are equivalent to two right angles, so that in the Dodecahedron there are contained, by power, **360 right angles**.

# In the Defense against Analysis XII.

...any of the elements could endure for even a moment of time, since according to Saint John <note>John 1:3</note>, all things were made through the **Word**, and without it, nothing was made; for in it was life, etc. And Saint Peter acknowledges that by means of this same **Word**, the heavens and the earth were created out of the waters and through the waters. But this great mystery of the **Word**, or the **Angelic Bread**, or the **Spiritual Rock**, and its unspeakable secrets, I commend to be explored and unraveled by those most enlightened and highly revered men, the **Brothers of the Rose Cross** <note>The Rosicrucians, a mysterious fraternal order Fludd famously defended, though it is debated if he was a formal member</note> (who are not so named without reason); for it is they who, through their writings, acknowledge that they possess the keys to the mysteries of this divine bread and its function. Regarding these men, I warn and entreat you, Johannes <note>Johannes Kepler (1571–1630), Fludd’s primary intellectual rival</note>, that you speak with greater modesty in the future; on page 43, you seem to treat them not with pure speech, but rather with a discourse full of mocking laughter and contempt. For in truth, I would have you know that all the secrets of Nature are not yet subject to the capacity of either Johannes or Robert, however sharp their minds may be. Therefore, I pray you cease to afflict those men with your little biting insults, for they are, without a doubt, to be preferred by a thousand degrees over both Johannes and Robert in the mysteries of **Philosophy** and the profound and true knowledge of **Worldly Harmony**.

Therefore, with all ambition cast aside, and carried along by other humbler means—lest by approaching the heat of the Sun, like **Icarus**, the melting of the wax on my wings should cause the deep abyss to swallow me up—I shall emerge content to concern myself only with that **material bread**. For I have recognized nothing closer to that spiritual bread than this material bread, except for Man himself. Nor indeed did Christ join bread with the **Word** without reason, since He Himself deigned to grant this honor to material bread, choosing to offer it to the disciples in place of His own body at His Last Supper. And it is said in Luke 24 that they recognized Christ through the **breaking of the bread**. Indeed, we see almost all of Christendom contending among themselves over the hidden nature and disposition of this Bread. Therefore, being inclined to investigate its nature and mysteries, I have sought out the marrow and center of this creature step-by-step through a gentle **anatomization** <note>Fludd refers here to a symbolic or alchemical "dissection" of matter to find its essence</note>, and beyond my imagination or hope, I have discovered the admirable secrets of nature. From the very heart of this subject, I have extracted the fabric of the world and of my **Physics** (I confess); nonetheless, with a deeper and more solid contemplation still accompanying me, I recognize with Solomon that a more certain and infallible order and reason for the creation of the world exists within the **Word**, or the **Spiritual Bread**, or **Divine Wisdom**, as if in a mirror. First, therefore, I saw all things massed together and disturbed in a vast cloud. Second, **Waters** appeared, tinted with light, at the base of which I observed a very black mass deprived of all form, which I compared to the substance of the formless **Chaos**. Therefore, setting out to treat that substance, I did not cease to penetrate step-by-step with curious eyes even unto its center; and there at last I noticed **five Elements**, distinct in nature, substance, and quality. I extracted each one in turn, separated them from one another, purified them, and saw how one held dominion over another in place and dignity. What I experienced regarding each of them, I shall now say in a word.

In the **Element of Earth**, by the first experiment, I saw the reason why vegetable nature is as much within mineral nature as it is within animal nature. Second, I perceived the origin of internal heat in the Earth: namely, that it proceeds from a certain clear and fixed **salt**. Third, I listened to the cause of why the Earth is called the **Matrix** <note>The "womb" or originating source</note> and receptacle of the other four elements—namely, the **Quintessence** <note>The "Fifth Essence" or purest underlying spirit of matter</note> and the remaining sublunary things. Fourth, I saw what the <term>Archeus</term> <note>The "vital tool" or internal invisible artisan that directs growth and life</note> of Nature, or the **Central Sun**, truly is; and finally, what the "Earth without form and void" signifies.

In the **Element of Water**, first, I observed that a tiny portion of life dwells within it. Second, I saw that it leads toward destruction within itself rather than toward nutrition: hence I perceived that this element works with **Fire** toward putrefaction and ruin, just as **Air** works with the **fifth element** toward life and conservation. But nonetheless, I saw that this element, bound in peace by the bond of nature, contributes in some way to the cooling of a composition.

In the **Element of Air**, first, I observed that it is nothing other than a most pure and volatile **salt**. Second, I saw how Air was enclosed on every side within Water, to which it seems to supply the force of life. Third, I saw that Air is the chief cause of **vegetation** <note>Alchemical growth and vitality</note>, and how it acts toward vegetation; indeed, I was taught by experience that it even promotes vegetation in **iron**. Fourth, I saw an experiment by which I was instructed how multiplication is brought about in animal, vegetable, and mineral bodies. Fifth, I saw that from these sublunary things, Air is like a sperm or matter disposed to receive the luminous seeds or **Tincture of the Sun**, both visible and invisible: which I beheld happening in a very short space of time with these very eyes with which I write these things. The sixth experiment declared that this Air, thus extracted, was from the universal **World Spirit**, since it participated in water, fire, and the quintessence. Seventh, it was proven that all things were made from **atoms**, according to the opinion of the **Epicureans**. And by the final experiment, I gathered that this spirit always acts through purification in this world.

In the **Element of Fire**, led first by a sufficiently pregnant reason, I observed that it is the chief author and producer of corruption and putrefaction in sublunary nature: and it is ready to attract to itself blackness and sad, diabolical darkness, and consequently, to induce burning diseases and malignant **melancholy**; for this Element acts as much against and beyond nature as that ethereal Fire acts toward the sustenance of life and nature.

By this, we may approach the starting point (the **Monad** <note>The mathematical and philosophical concept of "The One" or absolute unity, representing God</note>) and God himself, the presiding ruler of Light. For without a doubt, sensible and corporeal things are made according to the patterns of insensible and spiritual things. And so, rising further up from the sun, I yearned to lay open the mysteries of the Soul and of the Angels, and I did not despair of finally reaching the very fountain of uncreated Light by this path.

These things, I say, (Johannes), I have observed in the very center of nature’s womb. From these, I have securely, safely, and without deception laid the foundations of my Philosophy. These are not enigmas, parables, or Symbols, as you claim, but are true and proven by certain demonstration—all the more so because they are confirmed everywhere by the High Priest Moses, the Holy Scriptures, and the doctrine of the ancient Philosophers. And although I may seem to "create" nothing in this, yet by your leave, it will be very easy for a Philosopher to conceive through this inquiry of ours what a creature is, how it is created, and from what worldly means it is constituted. ...from damp and dense air; yet it does not follow that once the air is dried, that salt, which was moist, is therefore lighter than it was before. To your second point, we say that air is far more subtle and consequently can penetrate bodies more easily than water, since water is thicker than air. And who doubts that porous bodies—to avoid a vacuum—are constantly prone to soaking up air? If that air becomes humid, it acts upon the salt in marble by moistening it, though not by making it dissolve away, as you claim. On this point, I would like to advise you that I am learned by experience: marble itself is filled with more natural salt than any other stone I know.

After this, you say there is more matter in a single drop of water than in a vast space of air—specifically, that which fills an entire room. Now indeed, Johannes speaks outside of his own element <note>A pun suggesting Kepler is out of his depth or expertise</note>, for I am instructed by chemical experience that air enclosed by itself in a glass bulb, with the gentle heat of a lamp placed beneath it, would condense into many little drops of water like dew. And yet, the proportion of air necessary for the size of that space was filling it. We who are experienced in Chemistry certainly concede that a hundred portions of air may converge into a single portion of water; however, it does not follow that the air of an entire bedroom produces nothing but a single drop of water.

## In Defense of Annex XIII.

Behold me here, that Robert, who as you say has until now hidden himself in the groves of his Hermes <note>A reference to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of Hermetic philosophy</note>; I am, I say, stepping forward into the mathematical arena. You see him here, prepared to defend his words and writings against all—whether it be Johannes himself or any of his listeners who cry out against my "unworthy work" or the smallest part of it—and ready to repel their insults.

First, therefore, you assert that I conclude, against the assertions of the Ancients, that musical consonances are incommensurable <note>term: incommensurable; magnitudes that have no common measure, like the relationship between the side and diagonal of a square</note>. You misunderstand me here, Johannes; I do not thereby do away with the geometric dogma regarding incommensurable proportions. Rather, I only seem to suggest that from a certain Physical—or even Mathematical—perspective, every interval (such as the tone, the **Fourth**, the **Fifth**, and the **Octave**) is divisible into its parts, since every measurement of motion is made through limits, just as numbers are measured by units and lines by points. Do I here refute any Geometric dogma? Or if Johannes imagines this is not true, he also denies that any proportion on the **monochord** <note>A one-stringed scientific instrument used to demonstrate the mathematical ratios of musical intervals</note> is divisible into parts—that is, into tones and semitones. After all, the **Fourth** is composed of three intervals (namely, two tones and a semitone), the **Fifth** consists of four, and the **Octave** is composed of the **Fourth** and the **Fifth** joined together. The Ancients acknowledged this division into lengths or intervals, and even without their agreement, the visual and infallible observation of the monochord testifies to this same fact. Take the incommensurability of consonances in your own fashion, then; as for me, it will suffice to have understood their commensurability in my way, with experience also supporting it.

Furthermore, you wrongly conclude that I said consonances are *named* by numbers; yet I do not blush to affirm that they are explained and distinguished from one another by proportional numbers by way of comparison. For example, the **Octave** <note>original: Diapason</note> stands in a **double proportion** (2:1), the **Fifth** <note>original: Diapente</note> in a **sesquialter proportion** (3:2) <note>term: sesquialter; a ratio of 1.5 to 1, or 3:2</note>, and so on. Similarly, we say the **Fourth** <note>original: Diatessaron</note> consists of four voices, the **Fifth** of five, and the **Octave** consequently of eight. Therefore, Johannes is not yet strong enough in the mathematical arena, seeing as he thinks he can overcome Robert with empty words; nor indeed have I yet been reduced to such straits that I must beg for the assistance of any Adversary.

Besides, you make a great distinction between "commensuration" <note>measuring together</note> and "connumeration" <note>counting together</note>, not considering in the least that every measurement must be made through motion, and that motion itself is nothing other than a multitude of units—just as every measurement is made on a line, which is nothing other than a "flow of points." Therefore, the difference between commensuration and connumeration is the same as that between an arithmetic unit and a geometric point, which in effect are the same thing.

After this, it pleases you to argue with me about the nature of "unity," which you say is a work of the mind, simple, and existing in the abstract. You seem to be quibbling with us, Johannes; for I am speaking of this or that unity—namely, of one real and concrete substance, by whose proportion this or that sound is produced. For example, I take a certain flat piece of wood and, with compasses adapted for this work, I divide it into nine equal parts. The first part, then, will be the dimension of a tone of the primary monochord, since the dimension of this space or interval will correspond to the proportion of a tone. And by this kind of measurement, the monochord is divided into other units, as was declared in the preceding pages. And my units are of this sort: not in the abstract, but in the concrete, just as among merchants "one pound" or "one crown" <note>original: scuta; a reference to the 'ecu' or shield-marked gold coins</note>, and so on.

But let us proceed further. I compare a **Tone** to the line of a **Triangle**, and I say (as you assert) that just as sides are multiplied in shapes, so also are tones heaped up in consonances. Is this "Robert’s Cimmerian darkness" <note>A proverbial expression for intense or thick darkness, from the mythical people who lived in perpetual mist</note> that Johannes seems to imply? And yet he himself writes that the origin of that tone and all other consonances comes from the sectioning of a string through the shapes of a circle. I respond that, in a certain comparative sense, I applied tones to the lines of a triangle, but not because I thought they originally originated from those same sides. Therefore, I advise the Reader to look diligently at the analysis of that context, so that he may draw the truth of this controversy from it.

Then afterward, you cry out with an open mouth:

> O Geometers, inquire accurately if there is any among your number who understands Robert’s preceding speech.

It is clear that the smaller intervals are simple. Indeed, has any Geometer dared to maintain with Johannes that parts are no more simple than the whole composed from them? Because...

# Robert Fludd’s Reply

Indeed, I believe it is hidden from no one skilled in either philosophy or geometry that a single sound is simpler than the concord of a **Fourth** <note>original: "Diatessaron"</note>, since the latter consists of two whole tones and a semitone; or a **Fifth** <note>original: "Diapente"</note>, rather than an **Octave** <note>original: "Diapason"</note>, which is composed of a Fourth and a Fifth combined.

In the following passage, I see Johannes burning with rage; therefore, until he experiences some cooling relief, I shall impose silence upon myself. In the meantime, I perceive him to be as far removed from his expected trophy of victory as I persist here securely, unshaken by the fear of his words.

### On the Defense of Analysis XIV.

You say that you have not spent effort in learning the mysteries of Nature from the fables of the Poets. And I easily believe it; your writings tell us that this assertion of yours is no fable. But whether your mathematical demonstrations are more certain than the truth hidden beneath the fables of the Poets—this is the labor, this is the task to depict <note>A play on Virgil's "Hic labor, hoc opus est" from the Aeneid, referring to a difficult task</note>.

### On Analysis XV.

This Analysis pertains to your own *Harmony*; therefore, I will impose silence on myself in this place.

### On Analysis XVI.

Here I perceive Johannes stimulated by some kind of anger, by whose burning vapor I find myself cooked and re-cooked—if I may use his own words. I believe that, having utterly neglected the terrestrial kitchen of the Chemists, he has long performed the office of a cook in that combustion and most full indignation of the sphere of Mars <note>In astrology, Mars is associated with heat, fire, and anger</note>. I gladly refer the reader to the subject of my own Analysis on this matter.

### On Analysis XVII.

What your equal or unequal geometric units may be does not interest me, as I am content with my own proper units. Furthermore, even if I were to dispute further with you concerning **formal numbers** <note>Numbers viewed as metaphysical essences or archetypes rather than just quantities</note>, it would be a vain business for me, as you are someone who either does not know, or will not seem to know, either the formal proportions in nature or the logic of **essential numbers** <note>The underlying numerical principles Fludd believes govern the soul and the cosmos</note>. If you do not know, then there is no disputing against the ignorant; if you do know but will not seem to know, then contention with the perverse is empty.

But as soon as you begin to treat the essence of a thing—namely, the quantities of the mind (if it has any dimensions)—you are immediately seized by a certain blast of ill-will and break out into insults against me. You seem to falsely allege your authority, **Proclus** <note>A 5th-century Neoplatonist philosopher whom Kepler admired</note>, as if he, joined together with you as his disciple, would cast away my "ripenings" and "perfections," as you call them, into <note>original Greek: "μέγα κῦμα βαρυφλοίσβοιο γενέθλης"</note> **the great wave of the loud-roaring generation** <note>A phrase used to describe the chaotic material world or the flux of birth and death</note>. When Proclus was alive among men, I was nowhere to be found; and now that I exist among men, do you know where I might find him, Johannes? And yet you are not ashamed to use his mouth, feigning that he judged falsely concerning Robert, who did not even exist when he was alive.

But perhaps you dream that the "genius" of Proclus is present with you right now, who, like a **Socratic Demon** <note>A guiding spirit or inner voice, as Socrates claimed to have</note>, instructs you concerning your desired goals. But you are deceived, my Johannes; your spirit is deceived regarding my ripenings and perfections. A **Cacodæmon** <note>An evil spirit or demon</note> is present with you and deceives you. Therefore, take care in the meantime, lest that spirit cast your imaginary demonstrations—which feign that real geometric circles and their parts exist in the indivisible mind—into **the great wave of the loud-roaring generation**.

I recognize your violence: for I see you intensified with wrath because of my true opinion concerning **formal unity**. Indeed, you make everything I have said into riddles and parables, which in truth are as clear and transparent to a diligent observer as your own Sun. Therefore, what follows in this Analysis of mine, I gladly commend to the judgment of a just judge; for if I were to stir up everything proposed and opposed by Johannes, it would perhaps be a weariness both to me and to the reader.

### On Analysis XVIII, XIX, XX.

In these parts of Johannes's Defense pertaining to my *Harmony*, I am so secure in my Analytical Discourse—fortified by my aforementioned description of the **monochord** <note>A one-stringed instrument Fludd used to map the intervals of the entire universe</note> and its application to the harmony of the world—that I hope it is explained clearly enough to the just reader that the points Johannes seems to bring against it in his Defense are of no weight.

### On Analysis XXI.

Here, Johannes, I could speak with you with a more certain effort and more apt reason than you spoke to me in Analysis 13, by saying that as long as you hid yourself in the groves of your Proclus, your reputation was safe enough. Now, after you step forth into the **Chemical arena** <note>The "palæstra Chymica," referring here to the laboratory or the study of alchemy</note>, you are so manifest to all those devoted to this profession that they will cry out that this part of your Defense is unworthy. And if I were to shell out the errors you have brought forth in this brief mention of the **three chemical principles** <note>Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury—the foundational elements of Paracelsian alchemy</note>, I would undoubtedly make you more and more resentful toward me and stray too far from my goal. Therefore, for the sake of my own quiet and convenience, it does not please me to uncover your fault in this place.

### On Analysis XXII, XXIII, XXIV.

This dispute of yours tends against the proportions of the action and passion of **Light with the Waters** which were alleged by me: in which I know well enough that my demonstrations are too certain for any opposition of yours to be able to [harm] them in any matter.
