In the Defense of Annals XXV.

...can cause harm. Therefore, let the reader look into those Analyses of mine, and through them, he will perceive the meaning and the intention of my mind, which is by no means far from the truth.

### On Annals XXV.

Regarding the fact that I have properly applied my **Monochord** <note>A single-stringed instrument used by ancient and Renaissance theorists to demonstrate the mathematical ratios of musical intervals</note> and its intervals (contrary to your opinion) to the levels of the world or nature in the world, I hope this has been explained more than enough to a wise man in the preceding pages. There, I also demonstrated that the position of the **semitone** belongs to that level of the world where Light most abounds; for light, on account of its subtle disposition, can be reduced and contracted into the smallest space. This is seen, namely, in the element of Fire, the sphere of the Sun, and the starry heaven—which is called a **living being** <note>original: "ζῶον" (zoon)</note> because of its life-giving and lucid virtue—and finally the sphere of the **Seraphim** <note>The highest rank of angels, associated with fire and light</note>, burning with the presence of God, the fountain of light and the ruler of fire. 

He commands me to name the terms of **counterpoint**. I say, therefore, that they are the **Alpha and Omega**, or the **Small Aleph and the Great Aleph** <note>original: "Aleph paruum & Aleph magnum"; the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, used here to represent the beginning and end of divine creation</note>. The middle point between them is that most perfect creature called the **Sun**, which sounds a **double octave** <note>original: "Diapason duplicem"</note> toward the unity of its creator. This denotes that the Sun is the most perfect of the heavenly creatures, to which **Man** responds among the composite beings in the animal kingdom, **Wheat** in the vegetable kingdom, and **Gold** in the mineral kingdom. 

Next, you ask about the difference of the musical "genres" in this mundane monochord. I respond according to the Platonists, and especially your own **Proclus** <note>A 5th-century Neoplatonist philosopher who wrote extensively on mathematics and music</note>, that the genre of this kind of melody is primarily **Diatonic**; I have explained the reason for this in the preceding sections. Furthermore, by the power of this song—following the opinion of the Royal Psalmist—the heavens, stars, waters, rains, sounding clouds, snows, thunders, winds, and all creatures are said to praise God the Creator and resonate His honors with a most high voice. Indeed, I say to you that a formula of this kind of song exists within the stars and planets themselves, but in no different a way than it exists in all other creatures, however small; although, on account of the smallness of the subject, this harmonic virtue does not shine forth as clearly to us. 

But you say that you are full of certainty in this matter: namely, that the seat of the semitone is marked by certain boundaries of nature, and that the difference of musical genres, the terms of counterpoint, etc., are expressed in the very motions of the planets. From this, you conclude that you have detected something more of divine works in your harmonies than I have in mine—I, who (as you imagine) indulge in private conceptions of the world confirmed by no sensory evidence. 

Truly, my dear **Johannes** <note>Johannes Kepler</note>, if you had changed from a **Mathematician** into a **Prophet**, I would perhaps grant you greater faith in this matter, and I would suspect myself, dreaming that all my secrets and my virtue (whether great or small) had been revealed and detected by you. But from what you have said, I know that you remain a mere Mathematician, and like **Endymion** <note>In Greek myth, a beautiful youth who was granted eternal sleep so the Moon goddess could visit him; Fludd is implying Kepler is a dreamer distracted by the moon/planets</note> or a lover of the Moon, you have perhaps seen in a dream things that do not truly exist. Why should we expect to find that Harmony from the motions of the seven Planets, which are far distant from us, when it is revealed with open eyes and without any hesitation in a single, tiny subject right here among us? 

But you cry out, as it says on page 46: *"When at last, Robert, will you put an end to your arbitrary naming?"* I respond that because all things are surrounded for you by the thick mists of ignorance, they seem "arbitrary" to you. Therefore, to explain mysteries—however true—to men troubled by unbelief would be to **throw pearls before swine**. 

But I will now produce you as a witness against yourself. On page 13, you acknowledge **Tycho Brahe** <note>The famous Danish astronomer whose data Kepler used</note> (whom you confess to have succeeded in part of your work) as a faithful guardian of silence in **Hermetic matters** <note>Alchemical or mystical secrets attributed to Hermes Trismegistus</note>; yet in mathematical matters, you make him open and clear to the common people, hinting that he devised no enigmas and handed down nothing in pictures. You say: *"He did not,"* you say, *"promise to teach celestial motions without quantities, nor did he disdain to help weaker minds."* 

But what, Johannes, does this story of yours tend toward (so that I may have you as my witness even now)? It shows that this **Hermetic Art** is so noble in respect to that **vulgar Mathematics** that the latter should be handed down and made public to the profane crowd, while the former must be hidden in the Sanctuary of God and His Nature, lest the **bread of the sons of men** (to speak with Christ) be thrown to the dogs, or **pearls to swine**. Tycho himself, refusing to commend or publish the mystery of nature to the profane, reserved it secretly for himself and those worthy of it; but he did not hesitate to proclaim the common mathematical art, in his own way, to the world and to men of every condition, as a thing not so worthy of concealment. 

Yet we call both of these "mathematical arts." The first is the **external** art of vulgar mathematicians and, as you yourself confess, must be demonstrated by quantities and quantitative dimensions. The second is the **internal** art of the **Hermeticists**; it is declared by **formal demonstration** <note>A proof based on the essential "form" or soul of a thing rather than its physical size</note> and by the observation of essences in their progress toward perfection. It is not declared by quantitative dimensions, for it is impossible for that divine form—moving in and from the center of creatures—to be measured by them, since it is infinite and cannot be grasped by any category, much less explained or bounded by mathematical dimensions. 

Therefore, just as the **Soul** is to be preferred to the **Body**, so also is **Occult and Formal Mathematics** to be preferred to that which is manifest and measured by quantities—namely, by lines, surfaces, or bodies. And here I would like to warn the reader that the **Seven Liberal Arts** as they are commonly understood are only shadows and external images, as it were, of those seven which depend on true wisdom. Whence it is written: *"Wisdom has built her house upon seven columns."* And elsewhere, the **Holy Spirit of discipline** is called the producer of true sciences. 

Therefore, all the vulgar sciences are nothing but copies of the internal and occult ones, just as the body is cast in the image of the soul, and the spirit is said to lie hidden beneath the **"letter that kills"** <note>A reference to 2 Corinthians 3:6: "the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life"</note>. Just as the body is usually measured by quantitative dimensions—namely, surfaces, lines, and points—so also the Soul has its own dimensions. These are more essential and truly substantial, being purely spiritual and so far removed from the nature of the body that they cannot be outlined or demonstrated by quantity, which deals with bodies or three-dimensional space. And although philosophers attempt to describe God and the Mind itself with the numbers of merchants or geometric dimensions, they do this in an **analogical and symbolic** manner. Thus we describe God through the algorithmic figures 1, 2, 3. And others say that Jupiter is comprehended in the number seven hundred...

# Reply of Robert Fludd

...to be perceived as accurately as possible. Some assign the **Monad** <note>The number one, representing unity or God</note> to God the creator, the **Dyad** <note>The number two, representing duality or matter</note> to matter, and the **Triad** <note>The number three, representing the first composite form</note> to form. Under these external numbers, they understand internal numbers, which are the true and "formal" numbers; these are the various visions of Light and darkness in the progression of nature. These must be perceived with admiration, as they say, by the spectators, through whom we discern the fundamental order of common numbers and the original logic of geometric figures. These are indeed nothing other than the steps of nature’s various progression toward a state of "more-than-perfection." For the observation and modeling of these, wise men invented the external Arts, and I will say this boldly: there has been no original invention in the world that did not have its beginning from this "Mirror of Justice," according to the saying: *Wisdom teaches all things.* But let me proceed to the rest, and now I turn the thread of my speech toward you.

*You say that you ought not now to wink quietly, but rather demonstrate your indignation, because you see me provoked by rivalry and driven off course by an injury (which you say I imagine for myself, because you gave God His due, performing your duty by distinguishing between what is yours and what is mine). You claim I am driven to take revenge for these small offenses, so that by splashing and defaming your work, I might wrap the very works of God in the longer-lasting shadows of ignorance, as far as lies within my power. Here, certainly, you have fashioned a very beautiful prelude for yourself, and you mix threats with an argument of piety most excellently. If these things please you, I indeed congratulate your will and the pleasure you find in it. But in the meantime, I would have you know this: Robert neither cares nor gives a straw <note>original: "flocci quidem pendere," a Latin idiom meaning "to not care a shred"</note> whether John winks, or looks at him with eyes wide open and a more terrible wrath. For I do not envy John his divinity any more than I envy his virtue; I do not envy the happiness of his virtue in mathematics, for it is either not worthy of the mark of my envy, or it is far more eminent than it. I do not see what in your work is so admirable; it is enough if what you have written is worthy of the praise of some. But as for your giving God His due, I think that was done as becomes a Christian man, and I advise you to continue in that. However, as to your giving God His due in that you performed your duty by "distinguishing between what is yours and what is mine": here you are indeed imagining things. Formal things are received more from God than corporeal things, if you consider the dignity of our Harmony and that philosophical peace and concord, rather than the litigation and brawling of a controversy born of comparison. Therefore, it seems to me you in no way appear to give God His due in this work, for God is appeased more by a formal sacrifice than a material one. And as for the idea that I have become angry or stomach-sick toward you because you did all those things—you are remarkably mistaken in this. I am not envious, I am not angry; on the contrary, I see and become more cheerful. Finally, God knows better than that I should wrap His works in the shadows of ignorance by defaming your work, simply because I liken the Harmony of John to vain chimeras represented in the air. For just as internal or "formal" things are closest to God, while external and corporeal things are remote from God, so too (I speak now according to the sentiment of the Holy Scriptures) the body is likened to shadows and darkness—that appearing thing which is not, whence it is corruptible—while the soul and mind are the true image and likeness of God. Thus I have said that John’s external doctrine of the world’s Harmony stands in relation to the truth as the letter to the spirit, or the body to the soul. Yet I cannot deny that his Harmony is laudable according to the respect of external and common **Mathematics** <note>original: "Mathesis"</note>, nor are his inventions or observations to be despised in the least. But I say it stands in relation to formal and original Mathematics as a shadow of a thing stands to its reality; it is a shadow (I say) of the truth, but not the truth itself. May John forgive me if I speak now with the mouth of truth, and let him find me far removed from flattery or recantation. But if you inquire what this occult truth is, or what its description is: by Hercules, even if I knew and were well-versed in it, you yourself, John, seem to warn me—following the example of **Tycho Brahe** <note>A famous Danish astronomer (1546–1601) whose precise observations were used by Kepler</note>—to reveal it as little as possible, since you declared him to be silent and quiet regarding the **Hermetic mystery** <note>The secret alchemical and spiritual knowledge attributed to Hermes Trismegistus</note>. Let it be sufficient to think this one thing: that I shall attempt to strip truth down to its shining garment with the most fit demonstrations (though in a somewhat metaphorical way) and indicate its steps tending toward the goal of "more-than-perfection" in a symbolic manner, yet one very close to the truth of nature.*

You bring forward many other things here of no great weight; to examine all of them precisely would perhaps be too long and tedious for the readers. Therefore, I refer them to the examination of my *Analysis*.

->**To Analysis XXVI.**<-

I will leave you here to your triumph and the monuments of your praises. Meanwhile, I wish only to warn you of this: the **Brothers of the Rosy Cross** <note>The Rosicrucians, a secret brotherhood of sages and alchemists whose manifestos had recently caused a sensation in Europe</note>, whom you say I have praised—and I acknowledge I still praise them—are surely greater (in my opinion) than those whom the reproaches of the malevolent could harm. Therefore, I would wish you to be silent (as was said in the preceding pages), and I advise you to close your "hard mouth." For the blast of envy is moved against them like the spirit of the winds against cliffs that cannot be moved by any violence. Thus little dogs are accustomed to bark from a distance, but they do not know how to bite. Oh, how robust in body John would be, how powerful and strong in spirit, if he could force these Brothers—most eminent in Philosophy and **Theosophy** <note>Divine wisdom</note>—to come out into the crowds of men by his mere nod! On the contrary, they are obedient neither to you (my dear John) nor to me, your Robert; subject to no one but God alone, they will undoubtedly not fail to come forward in public and reveal themselves to the world in their own time. Meanwhile, let both John and Robert remain content with their own conceptions, and let them cease to bring reproaches and insults without cause or reason against men who are (as it seems to me) a thousand times more learned, lest this intemperance of their tongue eventually bring them harm.

Following the previous section where Fludd defended his symbolic and mystical "formal" mathematics, he now addresses the reader one last time before offering a final, olive-branch epilogue to Kepler himself, attempting to bridge the gap between their two very different worldviews.</meta>

### Regarding the Apology to Analysis XXVII.

This part of John’s <note>Johannes Kepler's</note> *Apology* does not seem to differ much from the "same batch of dough" as the others; it is, I say, full of quarrels and material of no great importance compared to the rest, which is why I feel it should be omitted for the sake of brevity. But now at last, to you, most desired Readers, to you (I say), let it be right and honorable for me to extend the thread of this brief discourse. Although the insolence of certain envious and malevolent people is not to be endured, I ask you, most sincere men, to remain in the duty of your holy goodness through the common law of humanity. I entreat you to weigh everything—both in my *Analytical Demonstration* and in *Johannes Kepler's Apology*—in the scales of justice. And as you will find that Robert has not yet recanted anything explained in his Analysis, so also you will perceive (I hope) that he has handled John's mocking words <note>original: "cachinnosis"</note> in many places of his *Apology* lightly and with enough patience. You will see that he has brought nothing against John's honor nor the laws of his own *Harmony* <note>Fludd’s "Harmonia Mundi" or "World Harmony"</note> in this his Reply; rather, he has accomplished only that which especially suits a Philosopher: namely, to establish his own position against anyone's insults or slanders to the best of his ability, and to defend his words, supported by the pillar of demonstration, like a strong soldier of Minerva <note>The Roman goddess of wisdom and strategic war</note>. I therefore gladly commend myself and my cause to your judgments, fortified by equity.

### Epilogue to the most illustrious Man and most celebrated in *Mathematics*, Johannes *Kepler*.

Although, most illustrious Sir, the most fitting occasion presented itself for me to be stirred to a just indignation in various places of this your *Apology*—to be not a little angry, or indeed to rage according to the measure of your vehemence and fervor—yet behold! Just as by a magical whispering swift rivers are said to turn back, unanimous winds to cease blowing, and the violence of lightning to be restrained, so also I hope you have found me until now sufficiently mild and steady. I am imbued with better moderation and patience, and the angry <note>original: "biliosum," referring to the humor of yellow bile associated with fire and anger</note> element in my very heart, however mobile and rapid it may be in itself, has been appeased by the spirit of your equanimity and offered friendship. I would show to you and to the learned of the world that I have never pursued your glory in *Mathematics* <note>original: "Mathesi"</note> or your virtue in *Philosophy* (whatever it may be) with rivalry or envy; rather, I have attempted in the preceding pages to support what is mine as if on Atlantic shoulders <note>Referring to the Titan Atlas, who held up the celestial spheres</note>. However, how much my soul is disposed toward peace and literary friendship, how remote from the perplexed contentions of debaters, and how inclined toward the contemplation of God and His Nature, I believe has been explained to you more than enough in the *Letter* annexed to the beginning of this little Treatise. 

I pray, therefore, most distinguished Sir, that you may be happy and favored in your mathematical studies, both private and public. I suggest you abstain from *Robert's Philosophy*. In this way, we shall confirm and kindly untie the firm bond and knot of philosophical friendship between us in the future; thus we shall break and release the strong chains of our contention and quarreling. With the right hand of friendship thus extended between us in one mind, let us finally enter into a perpetual treaty and pact, if it pleases you, by which that holy spirit of discipline—the lover of concord and instructor of true science—may lead us by his favorable breath into the way of truth. By his mediation, may we happily reach the longed-for goal of supreme wisdom.

->Farewell, December 9th, in the Year 1621.<-
